The hajj has its months; whoever commits to it in them must keep clear of sexual contact, vicious talk and disputing, and the verse turns from the provision a traveller packs to the provision he becomes: the best provision is Godwariness.

Three habits are then corrected. Trading in the season is no sin: al-Tusi calls the verse an explicit permission for commerce during ihram, which people had scrupled at in early Islam, and reports this from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq [18]. The standing is no privilege of the sanctuary's own: al-Tabrisi records that the command is addressed to Quraysh and their allies, the Hums, who would not stand with the people at Arafat nor stream out from it [6]. And the boasting has to stop: al-Baqir says that when the rites were done they would gather and count over their fathers' glories, so God ordered them to remember Him in that place instead [7]. Remembrance carries on into the appointed days, and two prayers are then set side by side, the one that asks only for this world and the one that asks for both.

From verse 204 the passage sorts people again. Tabatabai notes that the earlier verses divided them by what they ask for, this world or the next, while these divide them by hypocrisy and sincerity of faith [2]. One man's talk impresses, and given power he ruins crop and stock; another sells his soul for God's pleasure. Al-Tabrisi records Ibn Abbas holding the three verses revealed about the man who makes a show of religion, al-Hasan about the hypocrites, al-Suddi about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq [11].

The command that follows gathers all of it: enter into submission whole. Tabatabai reads these verses as the way religious unity is kept [3], and al-Tabrisi glosses Satan's steps as leaving any part of Islam's law [14]. Those who will not enter are left waiting for the day the matter is decided.

note.en: Al-Tusi gives the months of hajj, with us, as Shawwal, Dhu al-Qada and ten of Dhu al-Hijja, on a report from al-Baqir [17].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل اشترط على الناس شرطا، و شرط لهم شرطا … يرجع لا ذنب له
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God, mighty and majestic, laid a condition upon the people and laid a condition for them … He returns with no sin upon him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الرفث الجماع والفسوق الكذب والسباب والجدال قول الرجل لا والله وبلى والله

text.en: Rafath is intercourse, fusuq is lying and abuse, and jidal is a man's saying, 'No, by God' and 'Yes, by God'.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يعني الرزق، إذا أحل الرجل من إحرامه و قضى نسكه، فليشتر و ليبع في الموسم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Umar ibn Yazid the seller of Sabiri cloth, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It means provision: when a man comes out of his ihram and has completed his rites, let him buy and sell in the season.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و كانت قريش تفيض من المزدلفة و هي جمع، و يمنعون الناس أن يفيضوا منها … يعني إبراهيم و إسماعيل و إسحاق في إفاضتهم منها، و من كان بعدهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, both from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Quraysh would stream out from Muzdalifah, which is Jam, and would keep the people from streaming out from it … it means Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq in their streaming out from it, and those who came after them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: أما قولك: أخبرني عن الناس. فنحن الناس، فلذلك قال الله تبارك و تعالى ذكره في الكتاب: { ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ } فرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) الذي أفاض بالناس
narrations.chain: Ibn Mahbub, from Abd Allah ibn Ghalib, from his father, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: As for your saying, tell me about the people: we are the people. That is why God said in His Book, 'Then stream out from where the people stream out.' It was the Messenger of God who streamed out with the people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما وقف بهذا الموقف أحد من الناس مؤمن ولا كافر إلا غفر الله له، إلا أنهم في مغفرتهم على ثلاث منازل … مؤمن غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر واعتقه من النار
narrations.chain: his father, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: No one has stood at this standing place, believer or unbeliever, without God forgiving him; only they are of three ranks in their forgiveness … a believer whose past and future sin God forgave, and whom He freed from the Fire.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: رضوان الله و الجنة في الآخرة، و المعاش و حسن الخلق في الدنيا
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God's good pleasure and the Garden in the Hereafter; livelihood and good character in this world.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: معناه أنه يحاسب الخلائق دفعة كما يرزقهم دفعة … كيف يحاسب الله الخلق ولا يرونه قال كما يرزقهم الله ولا يرونه

text.en: It means that He reckons all creatures at once, as He provides for them at once … He was asked: how does God reckon the creation when they do not see Him? He said: as God provides for them and they do not see Him.

note.en: The appointed days are the days of tashriq, three after the sacrifice; the well-known days are the ten of Dhu al-Hijja, which al-Tabrisi reports from the imams [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ليس هو على ان ذلك واسع إن شاء صنع ذا وإن شاء صنع ذا لكنّه يرجع مغفوراً له لا إثم عليه ولا ذنب له

text.en: It is not that he has latitude here, to do this if he wishes or that if he wishes; rather he returns forgiven, with no sin upon him and no fault.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: التكبير في أيام التشريق، من صلاة الظهر من يوم النحر إلى صلاة الفجر من اليوم الثالث، و في الأمصار عشر صلوات
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The takbir in the days of tashriq: from the noon prayer on the day of sacrifice to the dawn prayer of the third day, and in the towns, ten prayers.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أن الحرث في هذا الموضع: الدين، و النسل: الناس

text.en: The tillage in this place is the religion, and the progeny is mankind.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: يهلك الحرث والنّسل بظلمه وسوء سيرته

text.en: He destroys the tillage and the progeny by his injustice and his evil conduct.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: نزلت في علي (عليه السلام) حين بات على فراش رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)
narrations.chain: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Safwan, from Mahfuz ibn Bahr, from al-Haytham ibn Jamil, from Qays ibn al-Rabi, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: It was revealed about Ali when he passed the night on the bed of the Messenger of God.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: فهل فيكم أحد نزلت فيه هذه الآية: { وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ } لما وقيت رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) ليلة الفراش غيري
narrations.chain: a group, from Abu al-Mufaddal, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya, from Ahmad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Ghudani, from al-Rabi ibn Sayyar, from al-Amash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, raising it to Abu Dharr

text.en: Is there among you anyone about whom this verse was revealed - 'And among the people is he who sells his soul seeking the pleasure of Allah' - when I shielded the Messenger of God on the night of the bed, other than me?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في ولاية علي بن أبي طالب (عليه السلام) … لا تتبعوا غيره
narrations.chain: Abu Muhammad al-Fahham, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Harun, from Abu Abd al-Samad Ibrahim, from his father, from his grandfather Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who heard Jafar ibn Muhammad

text.en: Of 'Enter into submission, all together': in the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib … and of 'do not follow in Satan's steps': do not follow anyone other than him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: السلم: هو آل محمد، أمر الله بالدخول فيه، و هم حبل الله الذي أمر بالاعتصام به
narrations.chain: Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The submission is the Family of Muhammad. God commanded entry into it, and they are the rope of God which He commanded us to hold fast to.

note.en: Fayd Kashani reads the stumble as a stumble away from entering the submission, after the proofs establishing that what you were called to is the truth [51].
Al-Tabrisi reads the coming as the coming of God's command or His punishment, under a covering of cloud [16].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: يقول: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله بالملائكة في ظلل من الغمام، و هكذا نزلت … إن الله عز و جل لا يوصف بالمجيء و الذهاب، تعالى عن الانتقال، و إنما يعني بذلك: و جاء أمر ربك و الملك صفا صفا
narrations.chain: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his father, who asked al-Rida

text.en: It means: do they await anything but that God should bring them the angels in the shades of the clouds; thus it was revealed … God is not described by coming and going, exalted above movement; what is meant is that the command of your Lord comes, with the angels rank on rank.

perspectives.en: Verse 207 shows where the readings part. Al-Tabrisi reports, from al-Suddi from Ibn Abbas, that it came down about Ali when the Prophet fled to the cave and Ali slept on his bed [13]. Al-Tabari's reports take it more broadly: Qatada says it was revealed about the Muhajirun and the Ansar [65]. Qurtubi too records that it came down about Ali when the Prophet left him on his bed [87]. On the next verse al-Tabari prefers the sense enter into Islam entirely [66], while al-Tusi holds obedience the wider sense and places the wilaya under it [28].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: نزلت الآيات في حجة الوداع، آخر حجة حجها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، وفيها تشريع حج التمتع.

sources.gloss: The verses were revealed at the Farewell Hajj, the last hajj the Messenger of God performed, and in it the hajj of tamattu was legislated.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: غير أن تلك الآيات تقسمهم من حيث طلب الدنيا أو الآخرة، وهذه الآيات تقسمهم من حيث النفاق والخلوص في الإيمان

sources.gloss: Those verses divide people by whether they seek this world or the Hereafter, while these verses divide them by hypocrisy and sincerity in faith.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: سبع آيات كاملة تبين طريق التحفظ على الوحدة الدينية في الجامعة الإنسانية وهو الدخول في السلم

sources.gloss: Seven complete verses which set out the way to preserve religious unity in the human community, and that is entering into submission.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن المراد به الإفاضة من عرفات وأنه أمر لقريش وحلفائها وهم الحُمْس لأنهم كانوا لا يقفون مع الناس بعرفة ولا يفيضون منها

sources.gloss: What is meant is the streaming out from Arafat, and it is a command to Quraysh and their allies, the Hums, because they would not stand with the people at Arafat nor stream out from it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ما روي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع أنهم كانوا إذا فرغوا من الحج يجتمعون هناك ويعدّون مفاخر آبائهم ومآثرهم ويذكرون أيامهم القديمة وأياديهم الجسيمة فأمرهم الله سبحانه أن يذكروه مكان ذكرهم آباءهم في هذا الموضع

sources.gloss: What is narrated from Abu Jafar al-Baqir: when they had finished the hajj they would gather there and count over their fathers' boasts and glories and recall their old days and great deeds, so God commanded them to remember Him in place of remembering their fathers in that spot.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهي أيام التشريق ثلاثة أيام بعد النحر والأيام المعلومات عشر ذي الحجة عن ابن عباس والحسن وأكثر أهل العلم، وهو المروي عن أئمتنا.

sources.gloss: They are the days of tashriq, three days after the sacrifice, while the well-known days are the ten of Dhu al-Hijja, from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and most of the people of knowledge, and it is what is narrated from our imams.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس نزلت الآيات الثلاثة في المرائي لأنه يظهر خلاف ما يُبطن وهو المروي عن الصادق ع إلا أنه عَيَّن المعَنيّ به. وقال الحسن: نزلت في المنافقين. وقال السدي: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said the three verses were revealed about the one who makes a show of religion, since he displays other than what he hides, and that is narrated from al-Sadiq, except that he named the one intended. Al-Hasan said they were revealed about the hypocrites. Al-Suddi said they were revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: روى السدي عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت هذه الآية في علي بن أبي طالب حين هرب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المشركين إلى الغار ونام علي ع على فراش النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: Al-Suddi narrated from Ibn Abbas: this verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib when the Prophet fled from the polytheists to the cave and Ali slept on the Prophet's bed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي آثاره ونزعاته لأن ترككم شيئاً من شرائع الإسلام اتباع للشيطان

sources.gloss: That is, his traces and promptings, for your leaving anything of the laws of Islam is a following of Satan.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي هل ينتظرون هؤلاء المكذّبون بآيات الله إلا أن يأتيهم أمر الله أو عذاب الله وما توعدهم به على معصيته في ستر من السحاب

sources.gloss: That is, do these deniers of God's signs await anything but that God's command or His punishment, and what He threatened them with for disobeying Him, should come to them under a covering of cloud.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وأشهر الحجّ - عندنا - شوال، وذو القعدة، وعشر من ذي الحجة، على ما روي عن أبي جعفر (ع)

sources.gloss: The months of hajj, with us, are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qada and ten of Dhu al-Hijja, according to what is narrated from Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: هذه الآية فيها تصريح بالاذن في التجارة، ونحوها في حال الاحرام، لأنهم كانوا يتحرّجون بذلك في صدر الاسلام, على قول ابن عباس، وابن عمر، ومجاهد، وعطا، والحسن، وقتادة، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر، وأبي عبد الله (ع).

sources.gloss: This verse contains an explicit permission for trade and the like in the state of ihram, because they used to hold back from it in early Islam, on the word of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, Ata, al-Hasan and Qatada, and it is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والأمران جميعاً عندنا جائزان محتملان، وحملها على الطاعة أعم، ويدخل فيه ما رواه أصحابنا من أن المراد به الدخول في الولاية

sources.gloss: Both senses are admissible with us; taking it as obedience is the more general, and included in it is what our companions narrated, that what is meant is entering into the wilaya.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ما وقف بهذا الموقف أحد من الناس مؤمن ولا كافر إلا غفر الله له، إلا أنهم في مغفرتهم على ثلاث منازل … مؤمن غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر واعتقه من النار

sources.gloss: No one has stood at this standing place, believer or unbeliever, without God forgiving him; only they are of three ranks in their forgiveness … a believer whose past and future sin God forgave, and whom He freed from the Fire.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله عز و جل اشترط على الناس شرطا، و شرط لهم شرطا … يرجع لا ذنب له

sources.gloss: God, mighty and majestic, laid a condition upon the people and laid a condition for them … He returns with no sin upon him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يعني الرزق، إذا أحل الرجل من إحرامه و قضى نسكه، فليشتر و ليبع في الموسم

sources.gloss: It means provision: when a man comes out of his ihram and has completed his rites, let him buy and sell in the season.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و كانت قريش تفيض من المزدلفة و هي جمع، و يمنعون الناس أن يفيضوا منها … يعني إبراهيم و إسماعيل و إسحاق في إفاضتهم منها، و من كان بعدهم

sources.gloss: Quraysh would stream out from Muzdalifah, which is Jam, and would keep the people from streaming out from it … it means Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq in their streaming out from it, and those who came after them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: رضوان الله و الجنة في الآخرة، و المعاش و حسن الخلق في الدنيا

sources.gloss: God's good pleasure and the Garden in the Hereafter; livelihood and good character in this world.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: التكبير في أيام التشريق، من صلاة الظهر من يوم النحر إلى صلاة الفجر من اليوم الثالث، و في الأمصار عشر صلوات

sources.gloss: The takbir in the days of tashriq: from the noon prayer on the day of sacrifice to the dawn prayer of the third day, and in the towns, ten prayers.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أن الحرث في هذا الموضع: الدين، و النسل: الناس

sources.gloss: The tillage in this place is the religion, and the progeny is mankind.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزلت في علي (عليه السلام) حين بات على فراش رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)

sources.gloss: It was revealed about Ali when he passed the night on the bed of the Messenger of God.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: السلم: هو آل محمد، أمر الله بالدخول فيه، و هم حبل الله الذي أمر بالاعتصام به

sources.gloss: The submission is the Family of Muhammad. God commanded entry into it, and they are the rope of God which He commanded us to hold fast to.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يقول: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله بالملائكة في ظلل من الغمام، و هكذا نزلت … إن الله عز و جل لا يوصف بالمجيء و الذهاب، تعالى عن الانتقال، و إنما يعني بذلك: و جاء أمر ربك و الملك صفا صفا

sources.gloss: It means: do they await anything but that God should bring them the angels in the shades of the clouds; thus it was revealed … God is not described by coming and going, exalted above movement; what is meant is that the command of your Lord comes, with the angels rank on rank.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: الرفث الجماع والفسوق الكذب والسباب والجدال قول الرجل لا والله وبلى والله

sources.gloss: Rafath is intercourse, fusuq is lying and abuse, and jidal is a man's saying, 'No, by God' and 'Yes, by God'.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: معناه أنه يحاسب الخلائق دفعة كما يرزقهم دفعة … كيف يحاسب الله الخلق ولا يرونه قال كما يرزقهم الله ولا يرونه

sources.gloss: It means that He reckons all creatures at once, as He provides for them at once … He was asked: how does God reckon the creation when they do not see Him? He said: as God provides for them and they do not see Him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ليس هو على ان ذلك واسع إن شاء صنع ذا وإن شاء صنع ذا لكنّه يرجع مغفوراً له لا إثم عليه ولا ذنب له

sources.gloss: It is not that he has latitude here, to do this if he wishes or that if he wishes; rather he returns forgiven, with no sin upon him and no fault.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: يهلك الحرث والنّسل بظلمه وسوء سيرته

sources.gloss: He destroys the tillage and the progeny by his injustice and his evil conduct.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: عن الدخول في السلم { مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ } الحجج والشواهد على أن ما دعيتم إليه حق

sources.gloss: 'If you stumble' away from entering the submission, 'after the manifest proofs that have come to you' - the arguments and evidence that what you were called to is the truth.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن قتادة فـي قوله: { وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللّهِ } قال: الـمهاجرون والأنصار

sources.gloss: From Qatada on His words, 'And among the people is he who sells his soul seeking the pleasure of Allah': he said, the Muhajirun and the Ansar.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وأولـى التأويلات بقوله: { ادْخُـلُوا فِـي السِّلْـمِ } قول من قال: معناه: ادخـلوا فـي الإسلام كافة

sources.gloss: The soundest of the interpretations of 'enter into the silm' is the view of those who said it means: enter into Islam, all of you.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وقيل: نزلت في عليّ رضي الله عنه حين تركَه النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم على فراشه ليلة خرج إلى الغار

sources.gloss: It is said that it was revealed about Ali when the Prophet left him on his bed the night he went out to the cave.

essay.en: The passage opens by pointing at a record. Ask the Children of Israel how many signs they were given: the staff turned serpent, the white hand, the parted sea, the shading cloud, the manna and quails [12]. To change a blessing, al-Tabrisi explains, is to distort it, conceal it, or twist it to a sense it will not bear [6]; Tabatabai reads the warning that follows as a standing law rather than one nation's story [1]. Verse 212 names the cause: the world looks beautiful to those who refuse, so the comfortable ridicule the poor who believe. Ibn Abbas placed this among the chiefs of Quraysh who mocked Ibn Masud, Ammar, Bilal and Khabbab [7]. Then the horizon widens. Mankind was one community, prophets came with the Book, and the split came from the people who had received it, out of envy. Tabatabai separates two differences: the natural rivalry over the goods of life, which is why law was legislated at all, and the tearing of religion itself, which is aggression after the proof arrived [2]. Verse 214 turns on the reader. No one walks into paradise untried, and al-Tusi relays from al-Suddi and Qatada that it came down at the Trench, with the Muslims besieged in Medina [15]. Two answers close the passage: one to Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who asked what to give and to whom [10], and one to a community told that fighting is now prescribed, which al-Tabrisi reports the exegetes read as an obligation of sufficiency [11]. God knows, and you do not.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فمنهم من آمن، و منهم من جحد، و منهم من أقر، و منهم من أنكر، و منهم من يبدل نعمة الله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Among them is one who believed, one who denied, one who acknowledged, one who rejected, and one who changes the blessing of God.

note.en: Al-Tusi says polytheists mocked the Muslims because their means were slender, and reads 'above them' as rank: the Muslims in Illiyyin, the wicked in the Blaze [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان هذا قبل نوح امة واحدة، فبدا لله فأرسل الرسل قبل نوح … بل كانوا ضلالا، كانوا لا مؤمنين، و لا كافرين، و لا مشركين
narrations.chain: Yaqub ibn Shuayb, who asked Abu Abdillah

text.en: This was before Noah: one community. Then it appeared to God, so He sent the messengers before Noah. Asked whether they were upon guidance or upon error, he said: rather they were astray, neither believers nor unbelievers nor polytheists.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: بل كانوا ضلالا، و ذلك أنه لما انقرض آدم (عليه السلام) و صالح ذريته، بقي شيث وصيه لا يقدر على إظهار دين الله الذي كان عليه آدم (عليه السلام) و صالح ذريته، و ذلك أن قابيل توعده بالقتل، كما قتل أخاه هابيل، فسار فيهم بالتقية و الكتمان، فازدادوا كل يوم ضلالة
narrations.chain: Mas'ada, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Rather they were astray. When Adam and the righteous of his offspring had passed, Shith his successor could not make God's religion manifest, for Qabil threatened to kill him as he had killed his brother Habil. So he lived among them in concealment, and they grew more astray each day.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فما تمدون أعينكم؟ فما تستعجلون؟ ألستم آمنين؟ أليس الرجل منكم يخرج من بيته فيقضي حوائجه ثم يرجع لم يختطف؟ إن كان من قبلكم [من هو] على ما أنتم عليه ليؤخذ الرجل منهم فتقطع يداه ورجلاه ويصلب على جذوع النخل وينشر بالمنشار
narrations.chain: al-Fadl, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Khalid al-Aquli, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Why do you stretch out your eyes? Why do you hasten? Are you not secure? Does not a man among you leave his house, settle his needs and return unseized? Of those before you who were as you are, a man would be taken, his hands and feet cut off, crucified on palm trunks and sawn apart.

note.en: Al-Suddi held the verse abrogated by the obligation of zakat; al-Hasan held that it stands, and al-Tusi calls that stronger, since nothing proves abrogation [16].
Al-Qummi says this came down in Medina and abrogated the verse 'restrain your hands', which had come down in Mecca [18].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: الجهاد فرض على جميع المسلمين لقول الله تعالى: { كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ } فإن قامت بالجهاد طائفة من المسلمين وسع سائرهم التخلف عنه ما لم يحتج الذين يلون الجهاد إلى المدد، فإن احتاجوا لزم الجميع أن يمدوهم حتى يكتفوا
narrations.chain: Da'a'im al-Islam, from Ali

text.en: Jihad is an obligation upon all the Muslims, for God's words, 'Warfare has been prescribed for you.' If a party of the Muslims undertakes it, the rest may hold back, so long as those engaged do not need reinforcement; if they do, all must reinforce them until they suffice.

perspectives.en: On 'mankind were a single community' the two traditions read the first age differently. Al-Tabrisi relays from al-Baqir that before Noah people were one community upon the fitra of God, neither guided nor astray, until God sent the prophets [8]. Ibn Kathir prefers the report from Ibn Abbas that they held to the religion of Adam until they worshipped idols, when Noah was sent as the first messenger to the people of the earth, calling it sounder in chain and in meaning [33]. Al-Razi records that most verifiers hold that first community was united in faith and truth [45].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وهذه هي السنة الجارية من الله سبحانه من يبدل نعمة وأخرجها إلى غير مجراها فإن الله يعاقبه، والله شديد العقاب

sources.gloss: This is the standing way of God: whoever changes a blessing and turns it out of its course, God punishes him, and God is severe in retribution.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالاختلاف اختلافان اختلاف في أمر الدين مستند إلى بغي الباغين دون فطرتهم وغريزتهم، واختلاف في أمر الدنيا وهو فطري وسبب لتشريع الدين

sources.gloss: Difference is of two kinds: difference over religion, which goes back to the aggression of the aggressors and not to their nature, and difference over worldly life, which is natural and is the reason religion was legislated.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والتبديل هو أن يحرف أو يكتم أو يتأول على خلاف جهته كما فعلوه في التوراة والإنجيل وكما فعلوه مبتدعة الأمة في القرآن

sources.gloss: Changing is to distort, or to conceal, or to interpret against its proper sense, as they did with the Torah and the Gospel, and as the innovators of this community did with the Quran.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت الآية في أبي جهل وغيره من رؤوساء قريش بسطت لـهم الدنيا وكانوا يسخرون من قوم من المؤمنين فقراء مثل عبد الله بن مسعود وعمار وبلال وخباب ويقولون لو كان محمد نبيّاً لاتبعه أشرافنا عن ابن عباس

sources.gloss: The verse came down about Abu Jahl and other chiefs of Quraysh, for whom the world was spread wide, who mocked poor believers such as Abdullah ibn Masud, Ammar, Bilal and Khabbab and said, had Muhammad been a prophet our nobles would have followed him. From Ibn Abbas.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروى أصحابنا عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع أنه قال كانوا قبل نوح أمة واحدة على فطرة الله لا مهتدين ولا ضُلاَلاً فبعث الله النبيين

sources.gloss: Our companions narrated from Abu Jafar al-Baqir that he said: before Noah they were one community upon the fitra of God, neither guided nor astray, then God sent the prophets.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في عمرو بن الجموح وكان شيخاً كبيرا ذا مال كثير فقال يا رسول الله بماذا أتصدق وعلى مَنْ أتصدق فأنزل الله هذه الآية

sources.gloss: It came down about Amr ibn al-Jamuh, an aged man of much wealth, who said: Messenger of God, with what shall I give charity, and to whom? So God sent down this verse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأجمع المفسرون إلا عطاء إن هذه الآية دالة على وجوب الجهاد وفرضِه غير أنه فرض على الكفاية

sources.gloss: The exegetes, apart from Ata, agree that this verse indicates the obligation of jihad, except that it is an obligation of sufficiency.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والآيات البينات ما ذكرها الله تعالى: من قلب عصا موسى حية، ويده البيضاء، وفلقه البحر، وتغريق عدوهم من فرعون وأصحابه، وتظليلة عليهم الغمام، وإنزال المن والسلوى

sources.gloss: The manifest signs are those God mentioned: the turning of Moses' staff into a serpent, his white hand, the splitting of the sea, the drowning of their enemy Pharaoh and his men, the shading of the cloud over them, and the sending down of manna and quails.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أن قوماً من المشركين كانوا يسخرون من قوم من المسلمين، لأن حالهم في ذات اليد كانت قليلة، فأعلم الله تعالى: أن الذين اتقوا فوقهم يوم القيامة، لأن المسلمين في عليين، والفجار في الجحيم

sources.gloss: A group of the polytheists used to mock a group of the Muslims because their means were slender, so God made known that the Godwary are above them on the Day of Resurrection, for the Muslims are in Illiyyin and the wicked in the Blaze.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ذكر السدي، وقتادة، وغيرهما من أهل التفسير: أن هذه الآية نزلت يوم الخندق لما اشتدت المخافة، وحوصر المسلمون في المدينة، واستدعاهم الله الى الصبر، ووعدهم بالنصر

sources.gloss: Al-Suddi, Qatada and other exegetes mentioned that this verse came down on the day of the Trench, when fear grew severe and the Muslims were besieged in Medina, and God called them to patience and promised them victory.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وذكر السدي: أن هذه الآية منسوخة بفرض الزكاة. وقال الحسن: ليست منسوخة، وهو الأقوى، لأنه لا دليل على نسخها

sources.gloss: Al-Suddi mentioned that this verse is abrogated by the obligation of zakat; al-Hasan said it is not abrogated, and that is the stronger view, since there is no evidence of its abrogation.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وقوله { كتب عليكم القتال وهو كره لكم } نزلت بالمدينة ونسخت آية { كفوا أيديكم } التي نزلت بمكة

sources.gloss: His words, 'Warfare has been prescribed for you, though it is repulsive to you', came down in Medina and abrogated the verse 'restrain your hands', which had come down in Mecca.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فمنهم من آمن، و منهم من جحد، و منهم من أقر، و منهم من أنكر، و منهم من يبدل نعمة الله

sources.gloss: Among them is one who believed, one who denied, one who acknowledged, one who rejected, and one who changes the blessing of God.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: بل كانوا ضلالا، كانوا لا مؤمنين، و لا كافرين، و لا مشركين

sources.gloss: Rather they were astray: they were neither believers, nor unbelievers, nor polytheists.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الجهاد فرض على جميع المسلمين لقول الله تعالى: { كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ }

sources.gloss: Jihad is an obligation upon all the Muslims, for God's words: 'Warfare has been prescribed for you.'

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والقول الأول عن ابن عباس أصح سنداً ومعنى، لأن الناس كانوا على ملة آدم حتى عبدوا الأصنام، فبعث الله إليهم نوحاً عليه السلام، فكان أول رسول بعثه الله إلى أهل الأرض

sources.gloss: The first report from Ibn Abbas is sounder in chain and in meaning, for the people were upon the religion of Adam until they worshipped idols, so God sent Noah to them, and he was the first messenger God sent to the people of the earth.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: القول الأول: أنهم كانوا على دين واحد وهو الإيمان والحق، وهذا قول أكثر المحققين

sources.gloss: The first view is that they were upon one religion, namely faith and truth, and this is the view of most of the verifiers.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. al-hasan al-tusi

excerpt.text: ألستم آمنين؟ أليس الرجل منكم يخرج من بيته فيقضي حوائجه ثم يرجع لم يختطف؟

sources.gloss: Are you not secure? Does not a man among you leave his house, settle his needs, and then return without being seized?

essay.en:
The passage is a run of questions put to the Prophet, and every answer weighs one harm against another. The first comes out of a raid. Al-Qummi records that Abdullah ibn Jahsh's men fell on a Quraysh caravan at Nakhla, killed Ibn al-Hadrami and took the caravan on the first day of Rajab, one of the sacred months, and that Quraysh then wrote to the Prophet charging him with making the sacred month lawful [13]. Al-Tusi notes the dispute over who asked: al-Hasan, al-Jubbai and most commentators say it was the idolaters, faulting the Muslims for it, while al-Balkhi says it was Muslims wanting to know the ruling [8]. The answer grants that fighting in that month is grave, then sets beside it what the idolaters had done, barring men from God's way, disbelief, expelling the Sanctuary's people: persecution is graver than killing.

Reassurance follows for those who believed, migrated and waged jihad; al-Tabrisi reports that it came down for Ibn Jahsh's companions, after some supposed that, if they were clear of sin, they had no reward either [5]. Then wine and gambling, where profit is admitted and the sin outweighs it, and where the Kufans apart from Asim read 'much sin' for 'great sin' [6].

Spending is answered with the surplus, orphans with setting their affairs right rather than shunning them, and the passage ends where mixing must stop, at marriage, revealed, al-Tabrisi reports, when Marthad ibn Abi Marthad asked leave to marry Anaq, a woman he had known before Islam [7].

note.en: Al-Tabrisi glosses the failed works: habt is first a corruption in the bellies of grazing animals that eat a certain plant, and destruction was then named after it [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الفتنة هنا هنا: الشرك

text.en: The persecution here means idolatry.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كذبوا، هذا اليوم لليلة الماضية لأن أهل بطن نخلة حيث رأوا الهلال، قالوا: قد دخل الشهر الحرام
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, by his chain from Aban, from Umar ibn Yazid

text.en: They have lied. This day belongs to the night just past, for the people of Batn Nakhla, when they saw the crescent, said: the sacred month has begun.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi ties this verse to the one before it: punishment is named first and reward after, so that the servant stands between fear and hope [5].
Al-Mizan takes wine to be any liquid made for intoxication, named from covering because it covers the mind [2]; al-Tusi reports our narrations as taking maysir to be all gambling [10].

narrations.speaker: Abu al-Hasan
narrations.arabic: بل هي محرمة في كتاب الله … و أما الإثم: فإنها الخمرة بعينها، و قد قال الله عز و جل في موضع آخر: { يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu Ali al-Ashari, from one of our companions, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Ali ibn Yaqtin

text.en: Wine is indeed forbidden in the Book of God. As for sin, it is wine itself, for God said elsewhere: They ask you concerning wine and gambling. Say, there is a great sin in both of them, and some profits for the people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إنّ الخمر رأس كل إثم ومفتاح كل شر … كلما قومر عليه فهو ميسر

text.en: Wine is the head of every sin and the key to every evil. Whatever is gambled over is maysir.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما بعث الله نبياً قط إلا وفي علم الله تعالى أنه إذا أكمل له دينه كان فيه تحريم الخمر ولم يزل الخمر حراماً وإنما ينقلون من خصلة ثم خصلة ولو حمل ذلك عليهم جملة لقطع بهم دون الدين

text.en: God never sent a prophet without knowing that, once his religion was completed for him, it would carry the prohibition of wine. Wine never ceased to be forbidden; people are only moved from one trait to the next, for had it been laid on them all at once they would have broken off short of the religion.

note.en: Al-Tusi gives the sense as leave for what they had scrupled at, mixing with orphans in property, provided they seek the orphans' welfare, as al-Hasan and others said and our reports have it [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما أنزلت: { إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلماً إنما يأكلون في بطونهم ناراً وسيصلون سعيراً } أخرج كل من كان عنده يتيم وسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله في إخراجهم، فأنزل الله تعالى: { ويسألونك عن اليتامى.. }
narrations.chain: his father, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When 'Indeed those who consume the orphans' property wrongfully only ingest fire into their bellies' came down, everyone who had an orphan with him put him out, and they asked the Messenger of God about sending them away; so God sent down, 'And they ask you concerning the orphans.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: تخرج من أموالهم قدر ما يكفيهم، و تخرج من مالك قدر ما يكفيك، ثم تنفقه … أما الكسوة، فعلى كل إنسان منهم ثمن كسوته، و أما الطعام فاجعلوه جميعا، فإن الصغير يوشك أن يأكل مثل الكبير
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Take from their property what suffices them, and from your own what suffices you, then spend it. As for clothing, each of them bears the price of his own; as for food, make it common, for the small one will soon eat as much as the big one.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن كان دخولكم عليهم منفعة لهم فلا بأس، و إن كان فيه ضرر فلا
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh, by his chain from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili

text.en: If your entering upon them is of benefit to them, there is no harm in it; and if there is harm in it, then no.

note.en: Al-Tusi holds the prohibition general, covering marriage with any disbeliever, neither abrogated nor restricted [12]; Tafsir al-Qummi counts the first clause abrogated by 5:5 and the second still standing [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: يا أبا محمد، ما تقول في رجل يتزوج نصرانية على مسلمة؟ … فما تقول في هذه الآية: { وَٱلْمُحْصَنَـٰتُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ } [المائدة: 5]. قلت: فقوله: وَ لا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكاتِ نسخت هذه الآية. فتبسم ثم سكت.
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm

text.en: O Abu Muhammad, what do you say of a man who marries a Christian woman alongside a Muslim wife? Then what do you say of this verse, 'and the chaste women of those who were given the Book before you'? I said: 'Do not marry idolatresses' abrogated it. He smiled, then said nothing.

perspectives.en: The last verse divides the traditions. Al-Tusi gives the Shia reading: the prohibition is general, forbidding marriage with disbelievers of any kind, and the verse is neither abrogated nor restricted to some idolatresses [12]. Al-Tabari reports the other view, that it forbade every idolatress and was then abrogated for the women of the People of the Book by the verse of al-Maida [27], and al-Qurtubi records that Malik, al-Thawri and al-Awzai held this, while Qatada and Said ibn Jubayr read the wording as general but its intent as particular [34].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الخمر على ما يستفاد من اللغة هو كل مائع معمول للسكر، والأصل في معناه الستر، وسمي به لأنه يستر العقل ولا يدعه يميز الحسن من القبح والخير من الشر

sources.gloss: Wine, as the language yields, is every liquid made for intoxication, and the root of its meaning is covering; it is so named because it covers the mind and does not let it tell the fair from the foul or the good from the evil

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والحبط فساد يلحق الماشية في بطونها لأكل الحباط وهو ضرب من الكلأ

sources.gloss: Habt is a corruption that afflicts grazing animals in their bellies from eating al-hubat, a kind of pasture

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت الآية في قصة عبد الله بن جحش وأصحابه لما قاتلوا في رجب وقتل واقد السهمي ابن الخضرمي فظن قوم أنهم إن سلموا من الإثم فليس لـهم أجر

sources.gloss: The verse came down concerning the affair of Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his companions when they fought in Rajab and Waqid al-Sahmi killed Ibn al-Hadrami, and some supposed that if they were safe from sin they had no reward

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم إثم كثير بالثاء والباقون بالباء

sources.gloss: The people of Kufa apart from Asim read 'much sin' with a tha, and the rest with a ba

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فدعته امرأة يقال لـها عناق إلى نفسها فأبى وكانت خلة في الجاهلية فقالت هل لك أن تتزوج بي فقال حتى استأذن رسول الله فلما رجع استأذن في التزوج بها فنزلت الآية.

sources.gloss: A woman called Anaq invited him to herself and he refused, and she had been a friend in the days of ignorance; she said, will you marry me? He said, until I ask leave of the Messenger of God; and when he returned he asked leave to marry her, and the verse came down

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فقال الحسن، وغيره: هم أهل الشرك على جهة العيب للمسلمين باستحلالهم القتال في الشهر الحرام، وبه قال الجبائي، وأكثر المفسرين. وقال البلخي: هم أهل الاسلام، سألوا عن ذلك ليعلموا كيف الحكم فيه.

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan and others said: they were the idolaters, faulting the Muslims for holding fighting in the sacred month lawful, and al-Jubbai and most commentators said the same. Al-Balkhi said: they were the Muslims, asking so as to know the ruling

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والميسر: قال ابن عباس، وعبد الله بن مسعود، والحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وابن سيرين: هو القمار كله وهو الظاهر في رواياتنا.

sources.gloss: As for maysir, Ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn Masud, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatada and Ibn Sirin said it is gambling of every kind, and that is what appears in our narrations

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى الآية الاذن لهم فيما كانوا متحرّجون منه من مخالطة الأيتام في الأموال

sources.gloss: The sense of the verse is leave for them in what they had scrupled at, mixing with orphans in property

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهذه الآية على عمومها - عندنا - في تحريم مناكحة الكفار، وليست منسوخة ولا مخصوصة.

sources.gloss: This verse, with us, stands in its generality, forbidding marriage with disbelievers, and it is neither abrogated nor restricted

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: حمل عليهم عبدالله بن جحش فقتل ابن الحضرمي وأفلت أصحابه وأخذوا العير بما فيها وساقوها إلى المدينة وكان ذلك في أول يوم من رجب من أشهر الحرم

sources.gloss: Abdullah ibn Jahsh charged them and killed Ibn al-Hadrami, his companions escaped, and they took the caravan with what was on it and drove it to Medina; that was on the first day of Rajab, one of the sacred months

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لما أنزلت: { إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلماً إنما يأكلون في بطونهم ناراً وسيصلون سعيراً } أخرج كل من كان عنده يتيم وسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله في إخراجهم، فأنزل الله تعالى: { ويسألونك عن اليتامى.. }

sources.gloss: When 'Indeed those who consume the property of orphans wrongfully only ingest fire into their bellies, and soon they will enter the Blaze' came down, everyone who had an orphan put him out, and they asked the Messenger of God about sending them away; so God, exalted, sent down, 'And they ask you concerning the orphans'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: منسوخ بقوله: { والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم } وقوله { ولا تنكحوا المشركين حتى يؤمنوا } على حاله لم ينسخ

sources.gloss: It is abrogated by His word, 'and the chaste women of those who were given the Book before you', while His word 'do not marry idolaters until they embrace faith' stands as it is and is not abrogated

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الفتنة هنا هنا: الشرك

sources.gloss: The persecution here: idolatry

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: بل هي محرمة في كتاب الله … و أما الإثم: فإنها الخمرة بعينها، و قد قال الله عز و جل في موضع آخر: { يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْخَمْرِ وَٱلْمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ }

sources.gloss: Rather, it is forbidden in the Book of God ... As for sin, it is wine itself, and God has said in another place: They ask you concerning wine and gambling. Say, there is a great sin in both of them, and some profits for the people

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: تخرج من أموالهم قدر ما يكفيهم، و تخرج من مالك قدر ما يكفيك، ثم تنفقه

sources.gloss: You take from their property what suffices them, and take from your own property what suffices you, then you spend it

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يا أبا محمد، ما تقول في رجل يتزوج نصرانية على مسلمة؟ … فما تقول في هذه الآية: { وَٱلْمُحْصَنَـٰتُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ } [المائدة: 5]. قلت: فقوله: وَ لا تَنْكِحُوا الْمُشْرِكاتِ نسخت هذه الآية. فتبسم ثم سكت.

sources.gloss: O Abu Muhammad, what do you say of a man who marries a Christian woman alongside a Muslim woman? ... What do you say of this verse, 'and the chaste women of those who were given the Book before you'? I said: his word 'do not marry idolatresses' abrogated this verse. He smiled, then fell silent

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: إنّ الخمر رأس كل إثم ومفتاح كل شر

sources.gloss: In al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq, that he said: wine is the head of every sin and the key to every evil

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: فقال بعضهم: نزلت مراداً بها تـحريـم نكاح كل مشركة علـى كل مسلـم

sources.gloss: Some of them said: it came down intending the prohibition of marrying any idolatress to any Muslim

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وٱختلف العلماء في تأويل هذه الآية فقالت طائفة: حرّم الله نكاح المشركات في سورة «البقرة» ثم نسخ من هذه الجملة نساءَ أهل الكتاب فأحلهنّ في سورة «المائدة».

sources.gloss: The scholars differed over the interpretation of this verse. One party said: God forbade marrying idolatresses in Surah al-Baqara, then the women of the People of the Book were abrogated out of this statement and made lawful in Surah al-Maida

essay.en:
Medina put a question to the Prophet, and the passage answers it. Before Islam people there avoided eating, drinking and sitting with a menstruating woman; Tabrisi reports this occasion from al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Rabi and judges it the stronger account [4]. The answer withdraws intercourse and nothing else: al-Tusi holds that nothing of her is forbidden except the place of the blood [10]. Tabatabai reads 'hurtful' not as bare harm but as what comes upon a thing and does not suit its nature [1]. The next verse answers a Jewish claim about conception [5], then lifts the subject: 'send ahead for your souls' means the deeds stored up with God [5].

From bodies the passage turns to speech. God's name must not become the barrier to piety, Godwariness and peacemaking; Tabrisi reports this was revealed about Abdullah ibn Rawaha, who had sworn not to speak to his in-law nor reconcile him with his wife [6], and Tabatabai says God does not accept His name being made a pretext for withholding what He commanded [2]. Oaths that merely run off the tongue carry nothing; what the heart earns does [7].

The theme then narrows to one oath in particular, sworn in anger to injure a wife [14]. Four months are given, then return or divorce; al-Tusi holds the man must actually pronounce it, and a judge may hold him until he does [15]. The passage ends with the divorced woman counting three periods of purity [9], a waiting that guards lineage [3], her rights answering what is owed by her.

note.en: The Kufan reading apart from Hafs doubles the letter in 'till they are clean': not merely that the blood stops but that she purifies herself, which Mujahid and Tawus took as wudu, the Imami view [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سئل عن الصادق عليه السلام ما يحل لصاحب المرأة الحائض منها فقال كل شيء ما عدا القبل بعينه … وفي رواية فليأتها حيث شاء ما اتّقى موضع الدم

text.en: He was asked what is lawful to the husband of a menstruating woman. He said: everything except the place of intercourse itself. In another report: let him come to her where he wishes, so long as he avoids the place of the blood.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إذا أصاب زوجها شبق، فليأمرها فلتغسل فرجها ثم يمسها - إن شاء - قبل أن تغتسل
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: About a woman whose menstrual blood stops on her last days: if her husband is overcome by desire, let him tell her to wash herself, then he may touch her, if he wishes, before she bathes.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان الناس يستنجون بالكرسف الأحجار ثم احدث الوضوء وهو خلق كريم فأمر به رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وصنعه فأنزل الله في كتابه ان الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين

text.en: People used to cleanse themselves with cotton and stones. Then washing with water came in, a noble practice, and the Messenger of Allah ordered it and did it; so God revealed in His book: Indeed Allah loves the penitent and He loves those who keep clean.

narrations.speaker: Abu al-Hasan
narrations.arabic: إن اليهود كانت تقول: إذا أتى الرجل المرأة من خلفها خرج الولد أحول، فأنزل الله عز و جل: { نِسَآؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَّكُمْ فَأْتُواْ حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ } من خلف أو قدام، خلافا لقول اليهود، و لم يعن في أدبارهن
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mamar ibn Khallad, from Abu al-Hasan

text.en: The Jews used to say that when a man comes to a woman from behind, the child is born cross-eyed. So God revealed: 'Your women are a tillage for you, so come to your tillage whenever you like' - from behind or in front, against what the Jews said; and He did not mean in their rear passages.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وقال الصادق عليه السلام " أنى شئتم " أي: متى شئتم في الفرج والدليل على قوله في الفرج قوله تعالى { نساؤكم حرث لكم } فالحرث الزرع في الفرج في موضع الولد

text.en: 'Whenever you like' means: whenever you wish, in the place of tillage. The proof is His word, 'Your women are a tillage for you': the tillage is the sowing in the place where the child is.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِذَا دُعِيتَ لِصُلْحٍ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ فَلا تَقُلْ عَلَيَّ يَمِينٌ أَلا أَفْعَلَ
narrations.chain: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: About God's words 'Do not make Allah an obstacle, through your oaths, to being pious and Godwary, and to bringing about concord between people': when you are called to reconcile two people, do not say, I am under an oath not to do it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يَا سَدِيرُ مَنْ حَلَفَ بِاللهِ كَاذِباً كَفَرَ وَمَنْ حَلَفَ بِاللهِ صَادِقاً أَثِمَ إِنَّ اللهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ وَلا تَجْعَلُوا اللهَ عُرْضَةً لأيْمانِكُمْ
narrations.chain: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Salam al-Mutaabbid

text.en: O Sadir, whoever swears by God falsely has disbelieved, and whoever swears by God truthfully has sinned. God says: 'Do not make Allah an obstacle, through your oaths.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: اللَّغْوُ قَوْلُ الرَّجُلِ لا وَاللهِ وَبَلَى وَاللهِ وَلا يَعْقِدُ عَلَى شَيْ‏ءٍ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: What is unconsidered is a man's saying 'No, by God' and 'Yes, by God', when he binds himself to nothing by it.

narrations.speaker: Abu Jafar al-Thani
narrations.arabic: شَرَطَ لَهُنَّ فِي الْإِيلَاءِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ إِذْ يَقُولُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ فَلَمْ يُجَوِّزْ لِأَحَدٍ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ فِي الْإِيلَاءِ لِعِلْمِهِ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى أَنَّهُ غَايَةُ صَبْرِ الْمَرْأَةِ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Jafar al-Thani

text.en: He stipulated four months for women in the oath of abstention, since God says, 'For those who forswear their wives shall be a waiting of four months.' He allowed no one more, for He knew that is the limit of a woman's endurance away from a man.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الإيلاء هو أن يحلف الرجل على امرأته ألا يجامعها فان صبرت عليه فلها أن تصبر، فإن رفعته إلى الإمام أنظره أربعة أشهر ثم يقول له بعد ذلك أما أن ترجع إلى المناكحة وأما أن تطلق وإلا حبستك أبداً
narrations.chain: his father, from Safwan ibn Maskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The oath of abstention is that a man swears against his wife not to lie with her. If she is patient with him, that is hers to choose; if she brings him to the Imam, he grants him four months, then says: return to marriage, or divorce, or I imprison you for ever.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و عزم الطلاق أن يخلي عنها، فإذا حاضت و طهرت طلقها، و هو أحق برجعتها ما لم تمض ثلاثة قروء
narrations.chain: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Bukayr ibn Ayan and Burayd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah

text.en: The resolve of divorce is that he leaves her be; when she has menstruated and become pure he divorces her, and he has the better right to take her back so long as three periods have not passed.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: بنى حظيرة من قصب وجعل فيها رجل آلى من امرأته بعد أربعة أشهر وقال له إما ترجع إلى المناكحة أو أن تطلق وإلا أحرقت عليك الحظيرة

text.en: He built an enclosure of reeds and put in it a man who had forsworn his wife past four months, and said to him: either you return to marriage or you divorce, or I burn the enclosure over you.

note.en: It is not lawful for her to hide blood or a pregnancy in order to hurry the waiting to its end, or to injure the husband in his right of return [3].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: في الكافي عن الباقر عليه السلام قال الاقراء هي الاطهار … إنما القرء الطهر يقرى فيه الدم فتجمعه فإذا جاء المحيض دفعه

text.en: The periods are the periods of purity. The period is the purity, in which the blood is held back and gathered, and when the menses comes it drives it out.

narrations.speaker: Abu Jafar al-Thani
narrations.arabic: أما عدة المطلقة ثلاثة قروء فلاستبراء الرحم من الولد
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Jafar al-Thani

text.en: As for the waiting of the divorced woman, three periods, it is to establish that the womb is free of a child.

perspectives.en: On the three periods the readings part. Tabrisi gives the Imami view that the quru are the periods of purity, shared with Zayd ibn Thabit, Aisha, Ibn Umar, Malik, Shafi'i and the people of Medina [9], and the Imams define the period as the purity between two menses [29]. Al-Tabari records the exegetes dividing over the word [36], and Qurtubi names the camps: the people of Kufa hold the quru are the menses, on the authority of Umar, Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, while the people of Hijaz hold they are the periods of purity [46].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالظاهر ان الأذى هو الطارئ على الشيء غير الملائم لطبعه فينطبق عليه معنى الضرر بوجه

sources.gloss: What is apparent is that hurt is what comes upon a thing and does not suit its nature, so the sense of harm applies to it in a way.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فإن الله سبحانه لا يرضى أن يجعل اسمه ذريعة للامتناع عمّا أمر به من البر والتقوى والأصلاح بين الناس

sources.gloss: God, glory be to Him, does not accept that His name be made a pretext for refusing what He commanded of piety, Godwariness and peacemaking between people.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وهو حبس المرأة نفسها عن الازدواج تحذراً عن اختلاط المياه

sources.gloss: It is the woman withholding herself from marriage, as a guard against the mixing of seed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل كانوا في الجاهلية يتجنبون مواكلة الحائض ومشاربتها ومجالستها فسألوا عن ذلك فنزلت الآية عن الحسن وقتادة والربيع

sources.gloss: It is said that in the age of ignorance they avoided eating, drinking and sitting with a menstruating woman, so they asked about that and the verse came down: from al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Rabi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت ردّاً على اليهود حيث قالوا إن الرجل إذا أتى المرأة من خلفها في قبلـها خرج الولد أحول فكَذَّبهم الله عن ابن عباس وجابر

sources.gloss: It is said it came down refuting the Jews, who claimed the child would be born cross-eyed, and God gave them the lie: from Ibn Abbas and Jabir.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في عبد الله بن رواحة حين حلف أن يدخل على ختنه ولا يكلمه ولا يصلح بينه وبين امرأته

sources.gloss: It came down about Abdullah ibn Rawaha, when he swore that he would go in to his in-law and not speak to him, nor make peace between him and his wife.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: هو ما يجري على عادة الناس من قول: لا والله وبلى والله من غير عقد على يمين يقتطع بها مال ولا يظلم بها أحد عن ابن عباس وعائشة والشعبي، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله

sources.gloss: It is what runs on people's habit of speech, 'no by God' and 'yes by God', without binding an oath by which property is seized or anyone wronged: from Ibn Abbas, Aisha and al-Shabi, and it is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والمراد بالقروء الأطهار عندنا، وبه قال زيد بن ثابت وعائشة وابن عمر ومالك والشافعي وأهل المدينة

sources.gloss: What is meant by the periods, with us, is the periods of purity; Zayd ibn Thabit, Aisha, Ibn Umar, Malik, al-Shafii and the people of Medina said so.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وعندنا: لا يحرم منها غير موضع الدم فقط

sources.gloss: With us, nothing of her is forbidden except the place of the blood alone.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ويكون الحلف على الامتناع من الجماع على جهة الغضب، والضرار، وهو المروي عن علي (ع)، وابن عباس، والحسن

sources.gloss: The oath is one of abstaining from intercourse by way of anger and injury; this is what is narrated from Ali, Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: عزيمة الطلاق في الحكم - عندنا - أن يعزم، ثم يتلفظ بالطلاق … فان لم يفعل، حبسه حتى يطلق

sources.gloss: Resolving on divorce, in the ruling with us, is that he resolves and then pronounces the divorce; if he will not, the judge holds him until he divorces.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
sources.gloss: Tafsir al-Qummi on 2:223, reporting Imam al-Sadiq on the meaning of 'whenever you like'.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
sources.gloss: Tafsir al-Qummi on 2:226 to 227, on the oath of abstention and Amir al-Muminin's judgement.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani
sources.gloss: Al-Burhan on 2:222 to 223, narrations on the menstruating wife and on the tillage.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani
sources.gloss: Al-Burhan on 2:226, narrations on the four months and the resolve of divorce.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani
sources.gloss: Tafsir al-Safi on 2:222 to 223, narrations from Imam al-Sadiq on what is lawful and on keeping clean.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani
sources.gloss: Tafsir al-Safi on 2:227 to 228, narrations from Imam al-Baqir that the periods are the periods of purity.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: واختلف أهل التأويـل فـي تأويـل القُرء الذي عناه الله بقوله

sources.gloss: The exegetes differed over the meaning of the period that God intended by His words.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وٱختلف العلماء في الأقْرَاء فقال أهل الكوفة: هي الحِيَض … وقال أهل الحجاز هي الأطهار

sources.gloss: The scholars differed over the periods: the people of Kufa said they are the menses, and the people of Hijaz said they are the periods of purity.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni
sources.gloss: Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq on 2:224 and the oath that blocks a reconciliation.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni
sources.gloss: Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq to Sadir on swearing by God.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni
sources.gloss: Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq on the unconsidered oath in 2:225.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni
sources.gloss: Al-Kafi, Abu Jafar al-Thani on why the waiting in the oath of abstention is four months.

essay.en:
Divorce may be only twice, and after each the husband stands before two doors: honourable retention or kindly release. Tabatabai notes that talaq at root means untying a bond, borrowed then for releasing a woman from the tie of marriage [1]. Al-Tibyan records two views: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid took the words as the shape of a lawful divorce, one pronouncement in a period of purity and then a second; Urwa and Qatada took them as the count beyond which separation is final [5]. Of a kindly release, it reports the Prophet's answer to a man who asked where the third pronouncement was, and the view of al-Suddi and al-Dahhak, narrated also from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah, that it means letting the waiting period run out [5]. Nothing given to her may be taken back unless both fear they cannot maintain God's bounds; Majma al-Bayan notes a variant reading of that verb, and that 'if you fear' may address the rulers and jurists who see to people's affairs [2].

After a third pronouncement she is not lawful to him until she marries another, a case Majma traces to the wife of Rifaa [3]; al-Tusi finds in the wording that a woman contracts her own marriage [6].

The last verse returns to conduct: no taking a wife back to injure her by stretching out her waiting period [4], no treating God's signs as a joke, for even a divorce said in jest binds [7], and a closing call to remember the Book and wisdom sent down.

note.en: The divorce meant here is the revocable one, which is two, since the third is final; what she gives 'to secure her own release' is the ransom of khul, lawful for him to take and for her to give [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ يُطَلِّقُهَا تَطْلِيقَةً يَعْنِي عَلَى طُهْرٍ مِنْ غَيْرِ جِمَاعٍ بِشَهَادَةِ شَاهِدَيْنِ ثُمَّ يَدَعُهَا حَتَّى تَمْضِيَ أَقْرَاؤُهَا فَإِذَا مَضَتْ أَقْرَاؤُهَا فَقَدْ بَانَتْ مِنْهُ … وَ إِنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُرَاجِعَهَا أَشْهَدَ عَلَى رَجْعَتِهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَمْضِيَ أَقْرَاؤُهَا فَتَكُونُ عِنْدَهُ عَلَى التَّطْلِيقَةِ الْمَاضِيَةِ
narrations.chain: Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Jafar Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The divorce of the sunna is that he pronounces one divorce, in a period of purity without intercourse, before two witnesses, then leaves her until her waiting periods pass; once they pass she is separated from him. If he wants her back, he has the return witnessed before they pass.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أقرت بالميثاق الذي أخذ الله: { فَإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسَٰنٍ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abd al-Rahman, who heard Abu Jafar

text.en: Of a man when he marries a woman, he said: she has acknowledged the covenant God took, 'either an honourable retention, or a kindly release'.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا يحل خلعها حتى تقول والله لا أبر لك قسماً ولا أطيع لك أمراً ولا أوطين فراشك ولأدخلن عليك بغير إذنك فإذا هي قالت ذلك حلّ خلعها وحل له ما أخذ منها من مهرها وما زاد وهو قول الله تعالى فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: Her release for a ransom is not lawful until she says: by God, I will keep no oath to you, obey no command of yours, nor honour your bed, and I will admit whom you have not permitted. When she says that, what he takes of her dower is lawful.

note.en: Al-Tusi holds the second husband must be adult, married to her by a sound permanent contract, and the marriage consummated [6]. Tafsir al-Qummi reads 'if he divorces her' as the third divorce, the leave to return covering the first two [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هي التي تطلق، ثم تراجع، ثم تطلق، ثم تراجع، ثم تطلق الثالثة، و هي التي لا تحل لزوجها حتى تنكح زوجا غيره و يذوق عسيلتها
narrations.chain: al-Razzaz, from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sumaa, all from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir

text.en: She is the one who is divorced, then taken back, then divorced, then taken back, then divorced a third time. She is the one who is not lawful to her husband until she marries another husband and he tastes her sweetness.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى إِنَّمَا أَذِنَ فِي الطَّلاقِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فَقَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الطَّلاقُ مَرَّتانِ فَإِمْساكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسانٍ يَعْنِي فِي التَّطْلِيقَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ … لِئَلا يُوقِعَ النَّاسَ الاسْتِخْفَافُ بِالطَّلاقِ وَلا يُضَارُّوا النِّسَاءَ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Said al-Hamdani, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father

text.en: God permitted divorce only twice, saying: divorce may be only twice, then either an honourable retention or a kindly release, meaning at the third pronouncement. So she was forbidden to him, that people might not take divorce lightly and women not be harmed.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا، لأن الله تعالى يقول: { فَإِنْ طَلَّقَهَا فَلاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُ مِن بَعْدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ } و المتعة ليس فيها طلاق
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh in al-Tahdhib, by his chain from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdallah ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal

text.en: Asked whether a temporary marriage makes her lawful again to the first husband, he said: No, because God says 'and if he divorces her, there is no sin upon them to remarry', and temporary marriage has no divorce in it.

note.en: Tafsir al-Qummi: once he has divorced her he may not take her back if he does not want her; 'do not retain them maliciously' means do not hold them captive [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا ينبغي للرجل أن يطلق امرأته ثم يراجعها، و ليس له فيها حاجة، ثم يطلقها، فهذا الضرار الذي نهى الله عز و جل عنه، إلا أن يطلق ثم يراجع و هو ينوي الإمساك
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, by his chain from al-Bazanti, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is not fitting for a man to divorce his wife, then take her back when he has no need of her, then divorce her. This is the harm God has forbidden, unless he divorces and then returns to her intending to keep her.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: مكتوب في التوراة: من أصبح على الدنيا حزينا، فقد أصبح لقضاء الله ساخطا … و من قرأ القرآن من هذه الامة ثم دخل النار، فهو ممن كان يتخذ آيات الله هزوا
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Amr ibn Jumay, raised to Amir al-Muminin

text.en: It is written in the Torah: whoever rises grieving over this world has risen displeased with God's decree. And whoever of this community recites the Quran and then enters the Fire is one of those who took the signs of God in derision.

perspectives.en: The traditions part over what makes a thrice divorced woman lawful to her first husband again. Al-Tusi holds, as agreed among the scholars, that the second husband must be adult, married to her by a sound permanent contract, and that the marriage be consummated [6]; the narrations add that a temporary marriage will not do, since it carries no divorce [12]. Al-Qurtubi reports a wider spread: Said ibn al-Musayyab and those who followed him held the bare contract enough, the majority of jurists required intercourse, and al-Hasan required more than that [21].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أصل الطلاق التخلية عن وثاق وتقييد، ثم استعير لتخلية المرأة عن حبالة النكاح وقيد الزوجية

sources.gloss: The root sense of talaq is release from a bond and a tether; it was then borrowed for releasing a woman from the snare of marriage and the tie of wedlock.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة إلا أن يُخافا بضم الياء والباقون بفتحها … فإن خفتم مصروفاً إلى الولاة والفقهاء الذين يقومون بأمور الكافة

sources.gloss: Abu Jafar and Hamza read 'unless they be made to fear' with a damma, the rest with a fatha. And 'if you fear' may be directed to the rulers and jurists who see to the affairs of the public.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي قصة رفاعة وزوجته نزل فإن طلقها فلا تحل لـه من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره

sources.gloss: It was in the affair of Rifaa and his wife that 'and if he divorces her, she will not be lawful for him thereafter until she marries a husband other than him' came down.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { ولا تمسكوهن ضراراً } أي لا تراجعوهن لا لرغبة فيهن بل لطلب الإضرار بهن أما في تطويل العدة أو بتضييق النفقة في العدة

sources.gloss: 'Do not retain them maliciously' means do not take them back with no desire for them but to harm them, whether by lengthening the waiting period or by squeezing her maintenance during it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدهما - ما قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد: إن معناه البيان عن تفصيل الطلاق في السنة … والثاني - ما قاله عروة، وقتادة: إن معناه البيان عن عدد الطلاق الذي يوجب البينونة … وروي عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أن رجلاً سأله، فقال: الطلاق مرتان فأين الثالثة؟ فأجابه: أو تسريح باحسان. وقال السدي، والضحاك: هو ترك المعتدة حتى تبين بانقضاء العدة، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر، وأبي عبد الله (ع)

sources.gloss: One view, that of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, is that it sets out the procedure of divorce according to the sunna; the second, that of Urwa and Qatada, is that it states the number of divorces that make separation final. Of 'a kindly release' it is narrated that a man asked the Prophet where the third was, and he answered: 'or a kindly release'; while al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said it is leaving her until she is separated by the expiry of the waiting period, and that is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وصفة الزوج الذي تحل المرأة، للزوج الأول أن يكون بالغاً، ويعقد عليها عقداً صحيحاً دائماً ويذوق عسيلتها … يدل على أن النكاح بغير ولي جائز، وأن المرأة لها العقد على نفسها، لأنه أضاف العقد إليها دون وليها

sources.gloss: The husband by whom she becomes lawful to the first must be an adult, must contract her in a sound and permanent marriage, and must consummate it. And the wording shows that marriage without a guardian is permitted, and that a woman may contract for herself, since He attributed the contract to her and not to her guardian.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: من طلق لاعباً، أو أعتق لاعباً، فقد جاز عليه

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God said: whoever divorces in jest, or frees a slave in jest, it is binding upon him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني الطلاق الثالث، وقوله: { فلا جناح عليهما أن يتراجعا } في الطلاق الأول والثاني

sources.gloss: It means the third divorce; and 'there is no sin upon them to remarry' concerns the first and the second divorce.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال إذا طلقها لا يجوز له أن يراجعها إن لم يردها فيضربها وهو قوله ولا تمسكوهن ضراراً أي لا تحبسوهن

sources.gloss: He said: once he has divorced her it is not lawful for him to take her back if he does not want her and only means to strike her; that is His word 'do not retain them maliciously', that is, do not hold them captive.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أقرت بالميثاق الذي أخذ الله: { فَإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسَٰنٍ }

sources.gloss: She has acknowledged the covenant God took: 'either an honourable retention, or a kindly release'.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هي التي تطلق، ثم تراجع، ثم تطلق، ثم تراجع، ثم تطلق الثالثة، و هي التي لا تحل لزوجها حتى تنكح زوجا غيره و يذوق عسيلتها … و المتعة ليس فيها طلاق

sources.gloss: She is the one divorced, taken back, divorced, taken back, and divorced a third time; she is not lawful to her husband until she marries another husband and he tastes her sweetness. And a temporary marriage has no divorce in it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فهذا الضرار الذي نهى الله عز و جل عنه، إلا أن يطلق ثم يراجع و هو ينوي الإمساك … و من قرأ القرآن من هذه الامة ثم دخل النار، فهو ممن كان يتخذ آيات الله هزوا

sources.gloss: This is the harm God has forbidden, unless he divorces and then returns to her intending to keep her. And whoever of this community recites the Quran and then enters the Fire is one of those who took the signs of God in derision.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أي التطليق الرجعي إثنتان فان الثالثة باين … لا جناح على الرجل في أخذ ما افتدت به نفسها واختلعت ولا على المرأة في إعطائه

sources.gloss: That is, the revocable divorce is two, for the third is final. There is no sin on the man in taking what she gave to ransom and release herself, nor on the woman in giving it.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فقال سعيد بن المسيب ومن وافقه: مجرّد العقد كاف وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: لا يكفي مجرّد الوطء حتى يكون إنزال. وذهب الجمهور من العلماء والكافّة من الفقهاء إلى أن الوطء كاف في ذلك

sources.gloss: Said ibn al-Musayyab and those who agreed with him said the bare contract is enough; al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan said intercourse alone is not enough without emission; and the majority of the scholars and the body of jurists held that intercourse suffices.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى إِنَّمَا أَذِنَ فِي الطَّلاقِ مَرَّتَيْنِ … لِئَلا يُوقِعَ النَّاسَ الاسْتِخْفَافُ بِالطَّلاقِ وَلا يُضَارُّوا النِّسَاءَ

sources.gloss: God, blessed and exalted, permitted divorce only twice, so that people would not fall into taking divorce lightly and would not harm women.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ يُطَلِّقُهَا تَطْلِيقَةً يَعْنِي عَلَى طُهْرٍ مِنْ غَيْرِ جِمَاعٍ بِشَهَادَةِ شَاهِدَيْنِ

sources.gloss: The divorce of the sunna is that he pronounces one divorce, in a period of purity without intercourse, before two witnesses.

title.en: Remarriage, nursing and the widow's wait

essay.en:
The divorce rulings end by turning to the people they press on hardest: a woman whose waiting is over, a nursing child, a widow. Tabatabai glosses such waiting as the woman holding herself back from marriage so that lineages are not confused [1]. Once her term has run out, no one may stand in her way: ‘do not hinder them from [re]marrying their husbands, when they honourably reach mutual consent.’ Tabrisi reports that the verse came down about Maqil ibn Yasar, who barred his divorced sister from returning to her first husband, and holds that its address falls on the divorcing men themselves, who are not to take a wife back near the end of her term to harm her [2].

Then the child. Mothers suckle two full years, the father owing food and clothing ‘in accordance with honourable norms’, and neither parent is to be made to suffer through the child. Tusi finds two things declared in the verse, one recommended and one obligatory [7].

Then the widow: four months and ten days. Tafsir al-Qummi holds this abrogates the year of maintenance promised in 2:240, the abrogating verse set before the abrogated in the surah's arrangement [12].

The passage closes on what a man may say to a widow still counting her days. He may hint, since allusion is the opposite of plain speech [5], but he may not make troth secretly, nor resolve the marriage tie until the term is complete. What is left is what only God sees.

note.en: ‘That will be more decent and purer for you’: Tabrisi glosses purer as purer for your hearts from doubt, since barring a woman who loves a man may drive them to what God forbade [2].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: أي لا تحبسوهن … يعني إذا رضيت المرأة بالتزويج الحلال

text.en: On 'do not hinder them': that is, do not confine them. On 'from remarrying their husbands, when they honourably reach mutual consent': that is, when the woman is content with the lawful marriage.

note.en: On ‘on the [father’s] heir devolve [duties and rights] similar to that’, Tafsir al-Qummi holds it unlawful for the heir to harm the mother of the child in her maintenance and squeeze her [11].

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: ما من لبن رضع به الصبي أعظم بركة عليه من لبن أمّه

text.en: There is no milk with which an infant is nursed greater in blessing for him than his mother's milk.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا رضاع بعد فطام … الحولان اللذان قال الله عز و جل
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman

text.en: There is no suckling after weaning. I said: may I be your ransom, and what is weaning? He said: the two years that God, Mighty and Majestic, spoke of.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الحبلى المطلقة ينفق عليها حتى تضع حملها، و هي أحق بولدها إن ترضعه بما تقبله امرأة اخرى
narrations.chain: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The pregnant divorcee is maintained until she delivers her child, and she has the better right to nurse him for whatever another woman would accept.

note.en: Tusi holds that a pregnant widow waits the later of the two terms, the delivery of her child or the four months and ten days, as is reported from Ali [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam Abu Jafar the Second
narrations.arabic: فإن الله عز و جل شرط للنساء شرطا، و شرط عليهن شرطا … و علم أن غاية صبر المرأة الأربعة أشهر في ترك الجماع، فمن ثم أوجبه عليها و لها
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman

text.en: God stipulated something for women and stipulated something upon them. He knew that the utmost of a woman's patience is four months in leaving intercourse, and so He made it binding upon her and for her.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن أهل الجاهلية كان إذا مات زوج المرأة أحدت عليه امرأته اثني عشر شهرا، فلما بعث الله محمدا (صلى الله عليه و آله) رحم ضعفهن، فجعل عدتهن أربعة أشهر و عشرا، و أنتن لا تصبرن على هذا
narrations.chain: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Samaa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim

text.en: In the age of ignorance, when a woman's husband died she mourned him twelve months. When God sent Muhammad, He had mercy on their weakness and made their waiting four months and ten, and you will not endure even this.
