note.en: ‘Until the prescribed term is complete’: Tafsir al-Qummi reads the term written in the Book as her own count of four months and ten [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو الرجل يقول للمرأة قبل أن تنقضي عدتها: أواعدك بيت آل فلان. ليعرض لها بالخطبة. و يعني بقوله … التعريض بالخطبة، و لا يعزم عقدة النكاح حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi

text.en: It is a man saying to a woman before her waiting expires: I will meet you at the house of so-and-so, hinting to her at a proposal. By 'unless you say honourable words' He means hinting at a proposal, without resolving the marriage tie until the prescribed term is complete.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: المرأة في عدتها تقول لها قولاً جميلاً ترغّبها في نفسك ولا تقول إني أصنع كذا وأصنع كذا القبيح من الأمر في البضع وكل أمر قبيح

text.en: To a woman in her waiting you say a fine word, making her desire you, and you do not say I will do this and that, the ugly matter of intimacy, or anything ugly.

perspectives.en: The traditions divide over whom 2:232 addresses. Ibn Kathir takes it of guardians barring a divorced woman, and finds in it proof that a woman cannot give herself in marriage without a guardian [25]; Qurtubi argues the same from Maqil's sister, a previously married woman who still needed her brother [29]. Tusi replies that in Shia law no brother or cousin holds guardianship over her, she is her own guardian, so the prohibition falls on the divorcing husbands [6]. Razi, from within the Sunni tradition, reaches that same reading from the grammar: the condition addresses husbands, so its answer must too [33].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وهو حبس المرأة نفسها عن الازدواج تحذراً عن اختلاط المياه

sources.gloss: It is the woman holding herself back from marriage as a precaution against the mixing of waters.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في معقل بن يسار حين عضل أخته جملاء أن ترجع إلى الزوج الأول وهو عاصم بن عدي

sources.gloss: It came down about Maqil ibn Yasar, when he barred his sister Jamla from returning to her first husband, Asim ibn Adi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: التعريض ضد التصريح وهو أن تضمن الكلام دلالة على ما تريد

sources.gloss: Allusion is the opposite of plain statement: it is that you load your speech with an indication of what you want.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لأن عندنا أنه لا ولاية للأخ، ولا لابن العم عليها وإنما هي ولية نفسها، فلا تأثير لعضلها

sources.gloss: For with us there is no guardianship of the brother, nor of the cousin, over her; rather she is her own guardian, so her being barred has no effect.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية بيان لأمرين: أحدهما مندوب، والثاني فرض

sources.gloss: In the verse is a declaration of two matters: one of them recommended, and the second obligatory.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فان كانت حبلى، فعدتها أبعد الأجلين، من وضع الحمل أو مضى الأربعة أشهر، وعشرة أيام، وهو المروى عن علي (ع)

sources.gloss: If she is pregnant, her waiting is the later of the two terms, the delivery of the child or the passing of the four months and ten days, and this is what is reported from Ali.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فلا يحل للوارث أن يضار أم الولد في النفقة فيضيق عليها

sources.gloss: It is not lawful for the heir to harm the mother of the child in maintenance and squeeze her.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهي ناسخة لقوله … فقد قدمت الناسخة على المنسوخة في التأليف

sources.gloss: It abrogates His words [on the bequest of a year's maintenance], and the abrogating verse has been placed before the abrogated one in the arrangement.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي تعتد وتبلغ الذي في الكتاب أجله أربعة أشهر وعشراً

sources.gloss: That is, she keeps her count and reaches what the Book has set as its term: four months and ten.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أي لا تحبسوهن

sources.gloss: That is, do not confine them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا رضاع بعد فطام

sources.gloss: There is no suckling after weaning.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و علم أن غاية صبر المرأة الأربعة أشهر في ترك الجماع، فمن ثم أوجبه عليها و لها

sources.gloss: He knew that the utmost of a woman's patience is four months in leaving intercourse, and so He made it binding upon her and for her.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو الرجل يقول للمرأة قبل أن تنقضي عدتها: أواعدك بيت آل فلان. ليعرض لها بالخطبة

sources.gloss: It is a man saying to a woman before her waiting expires: I will meet you at the house of so-and-so, so as to hint to her at a proposal.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ما من لبن رضع به الصبي أعظم بركة عليه من لبن أمّه

sources.gloss: There is no milk with which an infant is nursed greater in blessing for him than his mother's milk.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: المرأة في عدتها تقول لها قولاً جميلاً ترغّبها في نفسك

sources.gloss: To a woman in her waiting you say a fine word, making her desire you.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وفيها دلالة على أن المرأة لا تملك أن تزوج نفسها، وأنه لابد في تزويجها من ولي

sources.gloss: In it is an indication that a woman does not have the power to give herself in marriage, and that a guardian is indispensable in marrying her.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: ففي الآية دليلٌ على أنه لا يجوز النكاح بغير وَلِيّ لأن أُخت معقل كانت ثيّباً

sources.gloss: In the verse is a proof that marriage without a guardian is not permitted, for Maqil's sister had been married before.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وقال بعضهم إنه خطاب للأزواج، وهذا هو المختار

sources.gloss: Some said it is an address to the husbands, and this is the chosen view.

essay.en:
These verses return to divorce and, halfway through, turn to prayer. Tabatabai reads them as rulings on divorce and the waiting period with something of the rulings of prayer set among them [1].

Blame is lifted from a man who divorces a wife he has not touched and settled no dowry for: al-Tabrisi says the sin is lifted so that nobody imagines such a divorce forbidden [2]. Al-Tusi records the provision, from Ibn Abbas and from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, as a servant, clothing or food, sized to the man's means [8]. Where a dowry was named, half of it stands, unless one side forgoes it; al-Tabrisi holds that 'someone in whose hand is the marriage tie' is the guardian, as narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, though others read it as the husband [3].

Then, abruptly, 'Be watchful of your prayers'. Majma reports that the verse came down when the noon prayer lay heaviest on the companions and only a row or two stood behind the Prophet [4]. Danger does not cancel the prayer but reshapes it, on foot or mounted; when safety returns God is remembered, which Majma reads as the prayer of safety, or as praise [5]. The widow's year in her husband's house follows, then a last word on provision, which Majma reports, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, is said to have come after some declared they would give only if they wished [7]. It closes on the mind: al-Tusi calls the intellect the knowledge by which one tells ugly from good [14].

note.en: The 'settled dowry' is the sadaq: al-Tabrisi says there is no dispute that the contract itself makes it due to her [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في الرجل يطلق امرأته، أ يمتعها؟ قال: نعم، أما يحب أن يكون من المحسنين، أما يحب أن يكون من المتقين؟
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning a man who divorces his wife: should he provide for her? He said: Yes. Does he not wish to be among the virtuous? Does he not wish to be among the Godwary?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: سألته عن الرجل يريد أن يطلق امرأته قبل أن يدخل. قال: يمتعها قبل أن يطلقها، فإن الله تعالى قال: { وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى ٱلْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى ٱلْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ }
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh, by his chain from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Jafar

text.en: I asked him about a man who wants to divorce his wife before consummating the marriage. He said: Let him provide for her before he divorces her, for God has said: 'Yet provide for them, the well-off according to his capacity and the poorly-off according to his capacity.'

note.en: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab read this verse as abrogating the provision commanded before it; al-Balkhi answered that the two verses address different women, so one does not cancel the other [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال: هو الأب أو الأخ أو الرجل يوصى إليه، و الذي يجوز أمره في مال المرأة، فيبتاع لها فتجيز، فإذا عفا فقد جاز
narrations.chain: Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: He is the father, or the brother, or the man to whom the matter is entrusted, or one whose disposal in the woman's property is valid, buying for her and she allows it. If he forgoes, it stands.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يأتي على الناس زمان عضوض، يعض كل امرئ على ما في يديه، و ينسى الفضل و قد قال الله عز و جل: { وَلاَ تَنسَوُاْ ٱلْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ } ينبري في ذلك الزمان أقوام يعاملون المضطرين، هم شرار الخلق
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A biting age will come upon people, in which every man bites down on what is in his hands and graciousness is forgotten, though God has said: 'do not forget graciousness among yourselves'. In that age men step forward who trade on the desperate; they are the worst of creation.

note.en: Al-Qummi reports the Imam reciting 'the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer' [17]. Majma and al-Tusi still report from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that the middle prayer is the noon prayer [4][10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: و قال الله تعالى: { حَافِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وٱلصَّلَٰوةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ } ، و هي صلاة الظهر، و هي أول صلاة صلاها رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، و هي وسط النهار، و وسط صلاتين بالنهار: صلاة الغداة، و صلاة العصر
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God said: 'Be watchful of your prayers, and the middle prayer.' It is the noon prayer. It is the first prayer the Messenger of God prayed, it is the middle of the day, and it stands between the two day prayers, the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه قرأ { حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى صلاة العصر وقوموا لله قانتين } فقوله { قوموا لله قانتين } قال إقبال الرجل على صلاته ومحافظته حتى لا يلهيه ولا يشغله عنها شيء
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: He recited: 'Be watchful of your prayers, and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, and stand in obedience to Allah.' Of 'stand in obedience to Allah' he said: it is a man's turning to his prayer and guarding it, so that nothing distracts or occupies him from it.

note.en: Al-Tusi writes that one alone in acute fear prays two units by gesture, the prostration lower than the bow, and reports that Ali prayed five prayers by gesture on the night of al-Harir [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ الله (عَلَيْهِ الْسَّلام) عَنْ قَوْلِ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجالاً أَوْ رُكْباناً كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي وَمَا يَقُولُ إِذَا خَافَ مِنْ سَبُعٍ أَوْ لِصٍّ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ يُكَبِّرُ وَيُومِىُ إِيمَاءً بِرَأْسِهِ
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abd Allah

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about the words of God, 'and should you fear, then on foot or mounted': how does he pray, and what does he say, when he fears a beast of prey or a robber? He said: He says the takbir and gestures with his head.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فات أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) و الناس يوما [بصفين]- يعني صلاة الظهر و العصر و المغرب و العشاء- فأمرهم أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) أن يسبحوا و يكبروا و يهللوا قال: و قال الله: { فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجَالاً أَوْ رُكْبَاناً } فأمرهم علي (عليه السلام) فصنعوا ذلك ركبانا و رجالا
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Aban ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The Commander of the Faithful and the people missed the noon, afternoon, sunset and night prayers one day at Siffin, so he ordered them to glorify God, to magnify Him and to declare His oneness. God says: 'and should you fear, then on foot or mounted.' So they did that, mounted and on foot.

note.en: Al-Tusi holds the year of maintenance abrogated by the earlier verse setting four months and ten, while the bequest itself, in his view, remains as a recommendation [12].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وفي المجمع عن الصادق عليه السلام وفي عدة روايات عنه وعن الباقر عليهما السلام هي منسوخة نسختها يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشراً نسختها آيات الميراث

text.en: It is abrogated. 'They shall wait by themselves for four months and ten' abrogated it, and the verses of inheritance abrogated it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال: متاعها بعد ما تنقضي عدتها، على الموسع قدره، و على المقتر قدره، و كيف يمتعها و هي في عدتها، ترجوه و يرجوها، و يحدث الله بينهما ما يشاء؟!
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Her provision comes after her waiting period has ended, the well-off according to his capacity and the straitened according to his. How should he provide for her while she is still in her waiting period, when she hopes for him and he for her, and God may bring about between them what He wills?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أما إن الرجل الموسع يمتع المرأة بالعبد و الأمة، و يمتع الفقير بالحنطة و الزبيب و الثوب و الدراهم، و إن الحسن بن علي (عليهما السلام) متع امرأة طلقها بأمة، و لم يكن يطلق امرأة إلا متعها
narrations.chain: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Samaa, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The well-off man provides for the woman with a slave or a slave-girl, and the poor man with wheat, raisins, a garment and dirhams. Al-Hasan ibn Ali provided a slave-girl for a woman he divorced, and he never divorced a woman without providing for her.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما أدنى ذلك المتاع، إذا كان معسرا لا يجد؟ قال: خمار، أو شبهه
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: What is the least of that provision, when a man is destitute and finds nothing? He said: A headscarf, or something like it.

perspectives.en: The traditions divide over the middle prayer. Majma gives the noon prayer as the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Umar and Aisha, and as what is narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq [4]; al-Tusi records the same from the two Imams, while noting that the afternoon prayer was narrated from the Prophet, Ali and Ibn Abbas [10]. Al-Qurtubi, by contrast, gives the afternoon prayer as the choice of Abu Hanifa and his companions, of al-Shafi'i and most of the people of hadith, and quotes Ibn Atiyya that the majority hold it [42]. Ibn Kathir adds a line making it the dawn prayer, reported in Malik's Muwatta from Ali and Ibn Abbas [38].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات في احكام الطلاق والعدة وإرضاع المطلقة ولدها، وفي خلالها شيء من أحكام الصلاة

sources.gloss: An exposition of the verses on the rulings of divorce, the waiting period and a divorced woman's nursing of her child, and among them something of the rulings of prayer.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: هذا إباحة للطلاق قبل المسيس وفرض المهر فرفع الإِثم عن الطلاق قبل الدخول لئلا يتوهم أحد أن الطلاق في هذه الحالة محظور … والمراد بالفريضة الصداق بلا خلاف لأنه يجب بالعقد على المرأة فهو فرض لوجوبه بالعقد

sources.gloss: This is a permission for divorce before touching and before the dowry is settled; the sin is lifted from divorce before consummation so that nobody imagines divorce in this state forbidden. What is meant by the settled due is the dowry, with no dispute, since it becomes due to the woman by the contract.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل هو الولي عن مجاهد وعلقمة والحسن، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله … غير أن الأول أظهر وهو المذهب

sources.gloss: It is said that he is the guardian, from Mujahid, Alqama and al-Hasan, and that is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah. The first is the more evident, and it is the school's position.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: عن زيد بن ثابت أن النبي كان يصلي بالـهاجرة وكانت أثقل الصلوات على أصحابه فلا يكون وراءه إلا الصف أو الصفان … أحدها: أنها صلاة الظهر عن زيد بن ثابت وابن عمر وأبي سعيد الخدري وأسامة وعائشة وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله

sources.gloss: From Zayd ibn Thabit: the Prophet used to pray in the noonday heat, and it was the heaviest of prayers on his companions, so that only a row or two stood behind him. One view: it is the noon prayer, from Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Umar, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Usama and Aisha, and it is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { فإذا أمنتم } من الخوف { فاذكروا الله } أي فصلّوا صلاة الأمن وقيل اذكروا الله بالثناء عليه والحمد لـه

sources.gloss: 'And when you are safe' from fear, 'remember Allah', that is, pray the prayer of safety; and it is said: remember God with praise of Him and thanks to Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل لما نزلت { ومتعوهن على الموسع قدره } إلى قولـه { حقاً على المحسنين } قال بعضهم إن أحببتُ فعلت وإن لم أرد ذلك لم أفعل فأنزل الله هذه الآية عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

sources.gloss: It is said that when 'provide for them, the well-off according to his capacity' down to 'an obligation on the virtuous' came down, some of them said: if I like I will do it, and if I do not want to, I will not. So God sent down this verse. From Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومتعة التي لم يدخل بها ولا يسمى لها صداق على قدر الرجل، والمرأة، قال ابن عباس، والشعبي، والربيع: خادم أو كسوة أو رزق، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله (ع)

sources.gloss: The provision for a woman not consummated with and for whom no dowry was named is according to the means of the man and the woman. Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi and al-Rabi said: a servant, clothing or food, and that is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: روى سعيد بن المسيب: أن هذه الآية ناسخة لحكم المتعة في الآية الأولى. قال البلخي: وهذا ليس بصحيح، لأن الآية الأولى تضمنت حكم من لم يدخل بها، ولم يسم لها مهراً إذا طلقها، وهذه تضمنت حكم التي فرض لها صداق إذا طلقت قبل الدخول، وأحد الحكمين غير الآخر

sources.gloss: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab reported that this verse abrogates the ruling of provision in the first verse. Al-Balkhi said: this is not correct, because the first verse carried the ruling of the woman not consummated with and for whom no dowry was named, and this one carries the ruling of the woman for whom a dowry was settled and who is divorced before consummation; the two rulings are not the same.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { والصلاة الوسطى } هي العصر فيما روي عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وعلي (ع) وابن عباس، والحسن. وقال زيد بن ثابت، وابن عمر: إنها الظهر، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله (ع)

sources.gloss: 'And the middle prayer': it is the afternoon prayer, in what is narrated from the Prophet, Ali, Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan. Zayd ibn Thabit and Ibn Umar said it is the noon prayer, and that is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والذي نقوله: إن الخائف إن صلى منفرداً صلاة شدة الخوف صلى ركعتين يومىء إيماء، ويكون سجوده أخفض من ركوعه … وروي أن علياً (ع) صلى ليلة الهرير خمس صلوات بالايماء

sources.gloss: What we say is that one in fear, if he prays alone the prayer of acute fear, prays two units by gesture, his prostration lower than his bowing. It is narrated that Ali prayed five prayers by gesture on the night of al-Harir.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: هذه الآية منسوخة الحكم بالآية المتقدمة، وهي قوله: { والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجاً يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشراً } … فأما حكم الوصية، فعندنا باق لم ينسخ وإن كان على وجه الاستحباب

sources.gloss: The ruling of this verse is abrogated by the earlier verse, 'those of you who die leaving wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten'. As for the ruling of the bequest, in our view it remains and is not abrogated, though as a recommendation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والعقل مجموع علوم ضرورية يميز بها بين القبيح، والحسن، ويمكن معها الاستدلال بالشاهد على الغائب

sources.gloss: The intellect is the sum of necessary knowledge by which one distinguishes the ugly from the good, and with which one can reason from the seen to the unseen.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أنه قرأ { حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى صلاة العصر وقوموا لله قانتين } فقوله { قوموا لله قانتين } قال إقبال الرجل على صلاته ومحافظته حتى لا يلهيه ولا يشغله عنها شيء

sources.gloss: He recited: 'Be watchful of your prayers, and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, and stand in obedience to Allah.' Of 'stand in obedience to Allah' he said: it is a man's turning to his prayer and guarding it, so that nothing distracts him or occupies him away from it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نعم، أما يحب أن يكون من المحسنين، أما يحب أن يكون من المتقين؟

sources.gloss: Yes. Does he not wish to be among the virtuous? Does he not wish to be among the Godwary?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو الأب أو الأخ أو الرجل يوصى إليه

sources.gloss: He is the father, or the brother, or the man to whom the matter is entrusted.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و هي صلاة الظهر، و هي أول صلاة صلاها رسول الله

sources.gloss: It is the noon prayer, and it is the first prayer the Messenger of God prayed.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فأمرهم أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) أن يسبحوا و يكبروا و يهللوا

sources.gloss: So the Commander of the Faithful ordered them to glorify God, to magnify Him and to declare His oneness.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: متاعها بعد ما تنقضي عدتها، على الموسع قدره، و على المقتر قدره

sources.gloss: Her provision is after her waiting period ends, the well-off according to his capacity and the straitened according to his.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: هي منسوخة نسختها يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشراً نسختها آيات الميراث

sources.gloss: It is abrogated: 'they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten' abrogated it, and the verses of inheritance abrogated it.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فقيل إنها الصبح، حكاه مالك في الموطأ بلاغاً عن علي وابن عباس

sources.gloss: It is said that it is the dawn prayer, which Malik related in the Muwatta, without a full chain, from Ali and Ibn Abbas.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وممن قال إنها وسطى عليّ بن أبي طالب وٱبن عباس وٱبن عمر وأبو هريرة وأبو سعيد الخدريّ، وهو ٱختيار أبي حنيفة وأصحابه، وقاله الشافعي وأكثر أهل الأثر، وإليه ذهب عبد الملك بن حبيب وٱختاره ٱبن العربي في قَبَسِه وٱبن عطية في تفسيره وقال: وعلى هذا القول الجمهورُ من الناس وبه أقول

sources.gloss: Among those who said the afternoon prayer is the middle one are Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Abu Hurayra and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri; it is the choice of Abu Hanifa and his companions, and al-Shafi'i and most of the people of hadith said it. Abd al-Malik ibn Habib held it, and Ibn al-Arabi chose it in his Qabas, and Ibn Atiyya in his tafsir, who said: on this view are the majority of people, and I say it too.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: قَالَ يُكَبِّرُ وَيُومِىُ إِيمَاءً بِرَأْسِهِ

sources.gloss: He said: he says the takbir and gestures with his head.

title.en: The revived dead and Saul's kingship

essay.en:
Two scenes from the past frame one command to fight. A crowd leaves home in thousands to escape death, hears the word 'Die', and is revived. Tabrisi reports that they are said to have fled a plague, and that others held they fled a fighting prescribed for them [3]. Tabatabai reads 'Die' as a creative command that does not conflict with their dying by ordinary means, by the plague the reports mention [1]. For Tusi the verse urges fighting, since no flight avails against death [9].

The next verse commands fighting; the one after asks who will lend Allah a good loan, called a loan, says Tabatabai, because it is spent in His way [2].

The second scene answers the first. The elite of the Israelites ask their prophet for a king and promise to fight, then turn back, except a few, when fighting is prescribed. God appoints Saul, and they object: he is not of the house of kingship, and he has not been given ample wealth. Tabrisi notes that Saul was of the offspring of Benjamin, of neither the tribe of prophethood nor of kingship, and reads the reply, which names knowledge and physique, as setting a condition of the imam: that he be more knowledgeable than his flock [7]. Al-Balkhi, as Tusi reports, finds in the verse a refutation of holding leadership to be inherited [13]. The sign of his kingship is the Ark, borne by the angels: authority certified by what God gives, not by descent or wealth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: بل ردهم الله حتى سكنوا الدور، و أكلوا الطعام، و نكحوا النساء، و لبثوا بذلك ما شاء الله، ثم ماتوا بآجالهم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Hamran ibn Ayan, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Rather, God returned them until they dwelt in the houses, ate food and married women, and they stayed so as long as God willed; then they died at their appointed times.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن هؤلاء أهل مدينة من مدائن الشام، و كانوا سبعين ألف بيت، و كان الطاعون يقع فيهم في كل أوان … فلما قال حزقيل ذلك الكلام، نظر إلى العظام يطير بعضها إلى بعض، فعادوا أحياء ينظر بعضهم إلى بعض
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid and others, some of them from Abu Abd Allah and some from Abu Jafar

text.en: These were the people of a city of Syria, seventy thousand households, and the plague fell on them at every season. When Hizqil said those words, he saw the bones flying to one another, and they came back alive, looking at one another.

note.en: Tusi weighs who is addressed here and prefers the Companions over the revived dead, since on that reading the words stand as they are, with nothing left out [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما من شيء أحب إلى الله من إخراج الدراهم إلى الإمام، و إن الله ليجعل له الدرهم في الجنة مثل جبل احد … هو- و الله- في صلة الإمام
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Isa ibn Sulayman al-Nahhas, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Khaybari and Yunus ibn Zabyan

text.en: Nothing is more beloved to God than putting dirhams out to the Imam, and God makes that dirham in the Garden like the mountain of Uhud. By God, it is about giving to the Imam.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما نزلت هذه الآية على النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله): { مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهَا } [النمل: 89، القصص: 84] قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): اللهم زدني … فعلم رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أن الكثير من الله عز و جل لا يحصى، و ليس له منتهى
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz

text.en: When 'Whoever brings a good deed shall have better than it' came down, the Messenger of God said: O Allah, increase me. So the Messenger of God knew that the much which is from God cannot be counted and has no end.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فسلط الله عليهم جالوت، وهو من القبط فأذلهم وقتل رجالهم وأخرجهم من ديارهم وأموالهم واستعبد نساء‌هم … وكانت النبوة في بني إسرائيل في بيت والملك والسلطان في بيت آخر لم يجمع الله لهم الملك والنبوة في بيت واحد
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God set Goliath over them, and he was of the Copts; he humbled them, killed their men, drove them from their homes and their property, and enslaved their women. Prophethood among the Israelites was in one house and kingship in another; God did not gather the two in one house.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان الملك في ذلك الزمان هو الذي يسير بالجنود والنبي يقيم له أمره وينبئه بالخبر من عند ربه
narrations.chain: Majma al-Bayan and al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: In that age the king was the one who marched with the armies, while the prophet set his affair in order for him and brought him the news from his Lord.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: { فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوْاْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً مِّنْهُمْ }. قال: " كان القليل ستين ألفا
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sad ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: On 'So when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned back except a few of them': the few were sixty thousand.

note.en: Shaykh al-Saduq cites this verse to show that God may send a king who is neither messenger nor prophet, as Saul was [56].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إنّ الأنبياء والأئمة صلوات الله عليهم يوفقهم الله ويؤتيهم من مخزون علمه وحكمه ما لا يؤتيه غيرهم، فيكون علمهم فوق علم أهل الزمان … وقوله في طالوت وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Ala al-Hamdani, raising it, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim

text.en: God grants the prophets and the imams from the store of His knowledge and wisdom what He grants to no one else, so their knowledge is above the knowledge of the people of their age; and His word about Saul: 'Allah has appointed Saul as king for you.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: و كان أعظمهم جسما، و كان شجاعا قويا، و كان أعلمهم، إلا أنه كان فقيرا، فعابوه بالفقر
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He was the greatest of them in body, brave and strong, and the most knowing of them, except that he was poor; so they faulted him for his poverty.

note.en: Tabrisi holds the plain sense is that the tranquillity was a security and calm God placed in the Ark, so that the Israelites would find rest in it [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ثم قرأ أمير المؤمنين { بقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون } وأنا من رسول اله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمنزلة هارون من موسى، والعلم في عقبنا إلى أن تقوم الساعة
narrations.chain: Furat, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim ibn Ismail al-Anbari, from Hafs ibn Asim, Nasr ibn Muzahim and Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays

text.en: Then he recited, 'the relics left behind by the House of Moses and the House of Aaron', and said: I am to the Messenger of God as Aaron was to Moses, and the knowledge is in our posterity until the Hour rises.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: السكينة ريح من الجنة لها وجه كوجه الإِنسان فكان إذا وضع التابوت بين يدي المسلمين والكفار فإن تقدم التابوت لا يرجع رجل حتى يقتل أو يغلب
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Khalid, from al-Rida

text.en: The tranquillity is a wind from the Garden with a face like the face of a man. When the Ark was set between the Muslims and the disbelievers, if the Ark went forward no man turned back until he was killed or won.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وكان التابوت الذي أنزله الله على موسى فوضعته فيه أمه فألقته في اليم … قال البقية ذريّة الأنبياء
narrations.chain: al-Qummi, from al-Baqir

text.en: The Ark was the one God sent down upon Moses; his mother placed him in it and cast it into the sea. The remnant is the progeny of the prophets.

perspectives.en: Both traditions read the revival as a warning that flight does not escape death. The Shia commentators put it to a further use: Tabrisi and Tusi hold that reviving these people tells against anyone who denies the punishment of the grave and the raj'a, the return of the dead before the Judgment [3][9]. Ibn Kathir draws from the same event a lesson and a decisive proof of the bodily resurrection on the Day of Resurrection [31]. On Saul, Qurtubi reads the verse much as the Shia commentators do, making leadership deserved by knowledge, religion and strength rather than by lineage [39].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الأمر تكويني ولا ينافي كون موتهم واقعاً عن مجرى طبيعي كما ورد في الروايات ان ذلك كان بالطاعون

sources.gloss: The command is creative, and it does not conflict with their death coming about in the ordinary course, as the reports say it was by the plague.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وسماه إقراضاً لله لكونه في سبيله

sources.gloss: He called it a loan to God because it is spent in His way.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل هم من قوم بني إسرائيل وفرّوا من طاعون وقع بأرضهم عن الحسن، وقيل فرّوا من الجهاد وقد كتب عليهم عن الضحاك، ومقاتل … وهذه الآية حجة على من أنكر عذاب القبر والرجعة معاً

sources.gloss: It is said they were Israelites who fled a plague that fell on their land, from al-Hasan; and it is said they fled the fighting prescribed for them, from al-Dahhak and Muqatil. This verse is an argument against whoever denies the punishment of the grave and the raj'a together.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وكان طالوت من ولد بنيامين بن يعقوب ولم يكن من سبط النبوة ولا من سبط المملكة … وفيها دلالة على أن من شرط الإمام أن يكون أعلم من رعيته وأكمل وأفضل في خصال الفضل والشجاعة

sources.gloss: Saul was of the offspring of Benjamin son of Jacob, and was neither of the tribe of prophethood nor of the tribe of kingship. In it is an indication that it is a condition of the imam that he be more knowledgeable than his flock, and more excellent in the qualities of merit and courage.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والظاهر أن السكينة أمَنة وطمأنينة جعلـها الله فيه ليسكن إليه بنو إسرائيل

sources.gloss: The plain sense is that the tranquillity was a security and calm which God placed in it, so that the Israelites would find rest in it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى الآية: الحضّ على الجهاد، بأنه لا ينفع - من الموت - فرار … وفي الآية دليل على من أنكر عذاب القبر والرجعة معاً

sources.gloss: The meaning of the verse is urging to fight, since flight does not avail against death. In the verse is a proof against whoever denies the punishment of the grave and the raj'a together.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أنه متوجه الى الصحابة بعد ما ذكرهم بحال من فرّ من الموت، فلم ينفعه الفرار، حضهم على الجهاد … والقول الأول أظهر، لأن الكلام على وجهه، لا محذوف فيه

sources.gloss: One view is that it is addressed to the Companions, after reminding them of those who fled death and gained nothing by flight, urging them to fight. The first view is the more apparent, because the words stand as they are, with nothing left out.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال البلخي: وفي الآية دلالة على فساد قول من قال بأن الامامة وراثة

sources.gloss: Al-Balkhi said: in the verse is an indication of the falsity of the claim of those who say that the imamate is inherited.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وكانت النبوة في بني إسرائيل في بيت والملك والسلطان في بيت آخر لم يجمع الله لهم الملك والنبوة في بيت واحد

sources.gloss: Prophethood among the Israelites was in one house, and kingship and rule in another house; God did not gather kingship and prophethood for them in one house.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: السكينة ريح من الجنة لها وجه كوجه الإِنسان

sources.gloss: The tranquillity is a wind from the Garden with a face like the face of a man.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: بل ردهم الله حتى سكنوا الدور، و أكلوا الطعام، و نكحوا النساء، و لبثوا بذلك ما شاء الله، ثم ماتوا بآجالهم

sources.gloss: Rather, God returned them until they dwelt in the houses, ate food and married women, and they stayed so as long as God willed, then they died at their appointed times.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما من شيء أحب إلى الله من إخراج الدراهم إلى الإمام، و إن الله ليجعل له الدرهم في الجنة مثل جبل احد

sources.gloss: Nothing is more beloved to God than putting dirhams out to the Imam, and God makes that dirham in the Garden like the mountain of Uhud.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: { فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوْاْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً مِّنْهُمْ }. قال: " كان القليل ستين ألفا

sources.gloss: On 'So when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned back except a few of them': the few were sixty thousand.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: كان الملك في ذلك الزمان هو الذي يسير بالجنود والنبي يقيم له أمره وينبئه بالخبر من عند ربه

sources.gloss: In that age the king was the one who marched with the armies, while the prophet set his affair in order for him and brought him news from his Lord.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قال البقية ذريّة الأنبياء

sources.gloss: He said: the remnant is the progeny of the prophets.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: ثم قرأ أمير المؤمنين { بقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون } وأنا من رسول اله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمنزلة هارون من موسى، والعلم في عقبنا إلى أن تقوم الساعة

sources.gloss: Then the Commander of the Faithful recited 'the relics left behind by the House of Moses and the House of Aaron', and said: I am to the Messenger of God as Aaron was to Moses, and the knowledge is in our posterity until the Hour rises.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وكان في إحيائهم عبرة ودليل قاطع على وقوع المعاد الجسماني يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: In their revival was a lesson and a decisive proof of the occurrence of the bodily resurrection on the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فتضمّنت بيان صفة الإمام وأحوال الإمامة، وأنها مستحقة بالعلم والدين والقوّة لا بالنسب

sources.gloss: So it comprised a statement of the description of the imam and the conditions of the imamate, and that it is deserved by knowledge, religion and strength, not by lineage.

sources.author: abu abd allah muhammad b. ibrahim al-numani

excerpt.text: إنّ الأنبياء والأئمة صلوات الله عليهم يوفقهم الله ويؤتيهم من مخزون علمه وحكمه ما لا يؤتيه غيرهم، فيكون علمهم فوق علم أهل الزمان … وقوله في طالوت وَقَالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا

sources.gloss: God grants the prophets and the imams from the store of His knowledge and wisdom what He grants to no one else, so their knowledge is above the knowledge of the people of their age; and His word about Saul: 'Their prophet said to them, Allah has appointed Saul as king for you.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: وذو القرنين ملك مبعوث وليس برسول ولا نبي كما كان طالوت

sources.gloss: Dhu al-Qarnayn was a king sent by God, not a messenger nor a prophet, just as Saul was a king.

essay.en:
Saul marches out and, before an enemy is in sight, God sifts the army with a stream: whoever drinks is not his, whoever refrains is, barring one scoop of the hand. Tabatabai reads the story as told for believers newly commanded to fight, so they learn that rule and victory belong to faith and piety however few carry them [1]. The readers divide over the scoop itself, gharfah with a fatha or ghurfah with a damma [3]. In al-Safi the scoop becomes a figure: whoever kept to it found it enough, and so is this world to one bound for the Hereafter [19].

Most drink. The few cross, see Goliath's host, and hear from those certain of meeting God, 'How many a small party has overcome a larger party by Allah's will!' Facing the ranks they ask for patience, steady feet and victory. Then the sentence turns: they rout them, David kills Goliath, and kingdom and wisdom pass to a shepherd. The last clause widens past Israel: without God's repelling of people by one another the earth would be corrupted.

Tabrisi refers 'these are the signs' back over the whole sequence, thousands revived, Saul enthroned, the few victorious [6], and Tusi makes the telling itself the proof, since Muhammad witnessed none of it and knew none of its people [11]. It closes among the apostles, ranked by God, and Tabrisi says the ranking is stated so that no one levels them in merit merely because they are equal in messengership [7].

note.en: Tusi glosses 'will not belong to me' as: he is not upon my religion, nor of the people of my allegiance [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وروي عن أبي عبدالله عليه السلام أنه قال القليل الذين لم يشربوا ولم يغترفوا ثلثمائة عشر رجلاً

text.en: The few who neither drank nor scooped were three hundred and ten men.

narrations.speaker: Ibn Abbas
narrations.arabic: سماه نهراً فقال { إن الله مبتليكم بنهر } كما ابتلى بني إسرائيل … قتال جالوت فابتلاهم بنهر فابتلاكم بولاية علي
narrations.chain: Jafar ibn Ahmad, from Jafar ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Mazini, from Yahya ibn Rashid, from Kamil, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas

text.en: He named him a river, saying, 'Allah will test you with a stream,' just as He tested the Children of Israel when they went out to fight Goliath and tested them with a river. So He has tested you with the allegiance of Ali.

note.en: Tabrisi reads the request on the image of a vessel emptied out, the utmost that wisdom requires [4]; Tusi adds that patience is the servant's own act, while victory is God's [9].
Tusi records two readings of 'kingdom and wisdom': that kingship and prophethood were gathered for David at one time, or that he was singled out with a wisdom given to no one else [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله يدفع بمن يصلي من شيعتنا عمن لا يصلي من شيعتنا، و لو اجتمعوا على ترك الصلاة لهلكوا … و إن الله ليدفع بمن يحج من شيعتنا عمن لا يحج، و لو اجتمعوا على ترك الحج لهلكوا
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God repels through those of our Shia who pray from those of our Shia who do not pray; were they to agree on abandoning prayer, they would perish. And God repels through those of our Shia who make hajj from those who do not; were they to agree on abandoning hajj, they would perish.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: إن الله ليدفع بالمسلم الصالح نحو مائة ألف بيت من جيرانه البلاء
narrations.chain: al-Zamakhshari in Rabi al-Abrar, from Ibn Umar

text.en: Through the righteous Muslim God repels affliction from about a hundred thousand households of his neighbours.

narrations.speaker: Zayd ibn Ali
narrations.arabic: { تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ } و ما يعقلها إلا العالمون، قال زيد: نحن هم
narrations.chain: Furat ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Musa Sahib al-Aksiya

text.en: 'These are the signs of Allah, which We recite for you in truth' - and none understand them but those who know. Zayd said: We are they.

note.en: Tabatabai notes that what is between the prophets is called a preferring and ascribed to God, while what is among the people after them is called difference and ascribed to themselves [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: يا علي على ما تقاتل أصحاب رسول الله ومن شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمداً رسول الله؟ فقال على آية في كتاب الله أباحت لي قتالهم

text.en: Ali, on what ground do you fight the companions of the Messenger of Allah and those who testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah? He said: On a verse in the Book of Allah that has made fighting them lawful to me.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: سمهم بما سماهم الله عز وجل … فلما وقع الاختلاف كنا أولى بالله، وبدينه، وبالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، وبالكتاب، وبالحق. فنحن الذين آمنوا، وهم الذين كفروا
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Bilal al-Muhallabi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Hamid al-Lakhmi, from Sulayman ibn al-Rabi al-Nahdi, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Yahya ibn Yala al-Aslami, from Ali ibn al-Huzawwar, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata

text.en: Name them by what Allah named them in His Book. When the difference fell out, we were worthier of Allah, of His religion, of the Prophet, of the Book and of the truth: we are those who believed, and they are those who disbelieved.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَا ذَكَرَ مِنْ أَمْرِ السَّابِقِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ أَنْبِيَاءُ مُرْسَلُونَ وَغَيْرُ مُرْسَلِينَ جَعَلَ الله فِيهِمْ خَمْسَةَ أَرْوَاحٍ رُوحَ الْقُدُسِ وَرُوحَ الإيمَانِ وَرُوحَ الْقُوَّةِ وَرُوحَ الشَّهْوَةِ وَرُوحَ الْبَدَنِ … يَقُولُ أَكْرَمَهُمْ بِهَا فَفَضَّلَهُمْ عَلَى مَنْ سِوَاهُمْ
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, raising it, from Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Ghanawi, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali, who relays it from the Messenger of Allah

text.en: As for the foremost, they are prophets, messengers and others; God placed in them five spirits: the holy spirit, the spirit of faith, the spirit of power, the spirit of desire and the spirit of the body. He says: He honoured them with it and preferred them over all besides.

perspectives.en: The traditions part on the last verse. Fayd carries al-Ayyashi's report that Ali, asked on the Day of the Camel how he could fight men who said the takbir and prayed as his own side did, recited this verse and answered that we are the ones who believed and they are the ones who disbelieved [21]. Razi relays Abu Muslim's account, that the passage as a whole consoles the Prophet for the harm his people did him [41], and Ibn Kathir reads the fighting that followed the apostles as all of it Allah's decree and determination [31].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ثم يقص قصة طالوت وجالوت وداود ليعتبر بها هؤلاء المؤمنون المأمورون بالقتال مع أعداء الدين ويعلموا أن الحكومة والغلبة للإِيمان والتقوى وإن قل حاملوهما

sources.gloss: Then He tells the story of Saul, Goliath and David so that these believers, who are commanded to fight the enemies of the religion, may take a lesson from it and know that rule and victory belong to faith and piety even if those who carry them are few.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فسمى ما للأنبياء تفضيلاً ونسبه إلى نفسه، وسمى ما عند الناس بالاختلاف ونسبه إلى أنفسهم

sources.gloss: So He named what belongs to the prophets a preferring and ascribed it to Himself, and named what is among the people a difference and ascribed it to themselves.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأهل المدينة غَرفة بالفتح والباقون بالضم

sources.gloss: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and the people of Medina read gharfah with a fatha; the rest read it with a damma.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { علينا صبراً } أي وفقنا للصبر على الجهاد وشبهه بتفريغ الإناء من جهة أنه نهاية ما توجبه الحكمة

sources.gloss: 'Patience upon us' means: grant us patience in the struggle. He likened it to the emptying of a vessel, in that it is the utmost that wisdom requires.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { تلك } إشارة إلى ما تقدم ذكره من إماتة ألوف من الناس دفعة واحدة وإحيائهم دفعة واحدة بدعاء نبيهم

sources.gloss: 'These' points to what was mentioned before: the death of thousands of people at one stroke and their being brought to life at one stroke by the prayer of their prophet.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: إنما ذكر الله تفضيل بعض الرسل على بعض لأمور أحدها: لأن لا يغلط غالط فيسوّي بينهم في الفضل كما استووا في الرسالة

sources.gloss: God mentioned the preferring of some messengers over others for several reasons. One is so that no one should err and level them in merit as they are equal in messengership.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { فليس مني } معناه ليس على دينى، ولا من أهل ولايتي

sources.gloss: His words 'he is not of me' mean: he is not upon my religion, nor of the people of my allegiance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكذلك الصبر، لأنه من فعل العبد كما أن الثبوت في الحرب من فعله، لأنه يجازى عليه، فأما النصر، ففعل الله تعالى

sources.gloss: So too patience, since it is the servant's act, as standing firm in war is his act, for he is rewarded for it; as for victory, that is God's act.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قيل في معناه قولان: أحدهما - أنه جمع له الملك والنبوة في حالة واحدة. والآخر - أنه اختصه من علم السمع بحكمة لم يؤتها غيره

sources.gloss: Two views are given for its meaning: one, that kingship and prophethood were gathered for him at one time; the other, that he was singled out with a wisdom not given to anyone else.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما صارت الأخبار بذلك دلالة على النبوة من جهة أنها أخبار عن عيون لم تشهدها ولا خالط أهل المعرفة بها

sources.gloss: These reports became proof of prophethood only because they are reports of things he did not witness, and he never mixed with the people who knew them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وروي عن أبي عبدالله عليه السلام أنه قال القليل الذين لم يشربوا ولم يغترفوا ثلثمائة عشر رجلاً

sources.gloss: It is narrated from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: the few who neither drank nor scooped were three hundred and ten men.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يا علي على ما تقاتل أصحاب رسول الله ومن شهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمداً رسول الله؟ فقال على آية في كتاب الله أباحت لي قتالهم

sources.gloss: Ali, on what ground do you fight the companions of the Messenger of Allah and those who testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah? He said: on a verse in the Book of God that made fighting them lawful to me.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله يدفع بمن يصلي من شيعتنا عمن لا يصلي من شيعتنا، و لو اجتمعوا على ترك الصلاة لهلكوا … و إن الله ليدفع بمن يحج من شيعتنا عمن لا يحج، و لو اجتمعوا على ترك الحج لهلكوا

sources.gloss: God repels through those of our Shia who pray from those of our Shia who do not pray, and were they to agree on abandoning prayer they would perish. And God repels through those of our Shia who make hajj from those who do not, and were they to agree on abandoning hajj they would perish.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: { تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ } و ما يعقلها إلا العالمون، قال زيد: نحن هم

sources.gloss: 'These are the signs of Allah, which We recite for you in truth' - and none understand them but those who know. Zayd said: we are they.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وروي أن من اقتصر على الغرفة كفته لشربه وأدواته ومن لم يقتصر غلب عطشه واسودّت شفته ولم يقدر أن يمضي وهكذا الدنيا لقاصد الآخرة

sources.gloss: It is narrated that whoever confined himself to the scoop, it sufficed him for his drink and his gear, and whoever did not was overcome by thirst and his lip blackened and he could not go on; and such is this world for one bound for the Hereafter.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: والعياشي سئل عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام يوم الجمل كبر القوم وكبّرنا وهلل القوم وهللنا وصلّى القوم وصلّينا فعلى مَا نقاتلهم فتلا هذه الآية ثم قال نحن الذين من بعدهم وقال فنحن الذين آمنّا وهم الذين كفروا

sources.gloss: Al-Ayyashi: the Commander of the Faithful was asked on the Day of the Camel, the people said the takbir and we said it, they said the tahlil and we said it, they prayed and we prayed, so on what ground do we fight them? He recited this verse and said: we are those who came after them, and we are those who believed and they are those who disbelieved.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: سماه نهراً فقال { إن الله مبتليكم بنهر } كما ابتلى بني إسرائيل … قتال جالوت فابتلاهم بنهر فابتلاكم بولاية علي

sources.gloss: He named him a river, for He said, 'Allah will test you with a stream,' just as He tested the Children of Israel when they went out to fight Goliath and tested them with a river; so He has tested you with the allegiance of Ali.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: أي كل ذلك عن قضاء الله وقدره

sources.gloss: That is, all of that is by Allah's decree and determination.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وجه تعليق هذه الآية بما قبلها ما ذكره أبو مسلم … وبالجملة فالمقصود من هذا الكلام تسلية الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على إيذاء قومه له

sources.gloss: The way this verse connects with what precedes it is what Abu Muslim mentioned ... In sum, the purpose of this speech is to console the Messenger for the harm his people did him.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: فَأَمَّا مَا ذَكَرَ مِنْ أَمْرِ السَّابِقِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ أَنْبِيَاءُ مُرْسَلُونَ وَغَيْرُ مُرْسَلِينَ جَعَلَ الله فِيهِمْ خَمْسَةَ أَرْوَاحٍ رُوحَ الْقُدُسِ وَرُوحَ الإيمَانِ وَرُوحَ الْقُوَّةِ وَرُوحَ الشَّهْوَةِ وَرُوحَ الْبَدَنِ … يَقُولُ أَكْرَمَهُمْ بِهَا فَفَضَّلَهُمْ عَلَى مَنْ سِوَاهُمْ

sources.gloss: As for the foremost, they are prophets, messengers and non-messengers; God placed in them five spirits: the holy spirit, the spirit of faith, the spirit of power, the spirit of desire and the spirit of the body. He says: He honoured them with it and preferred them over all besides.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. muhammad al-mufid

excerpt.text: سمهم بما سماهم الله عز وجل … فلما وقع الاختلاف كنا أولى بالله، وبدينه، وبالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، وبالكتاب، وبالحق. فنحن الذين آمنوا، وهم الذين كفروا

sources.gloss: Name them by what Allah named them in His Book. When the difference fell out, we were worthier of Allah, of His religion, of the Prophet, of the Book and of the truth: we are those who believed and they are those who disbelieved.

title.en: The Throne Verse and true allegiance

essay.en:
The passage moves from a command, to a portrait of God, to the freedom of belief. Spend out of what We have provided you, before a day with no bargaining, friendship or intercession. Al-Tabrisi reports Hasan's view that only obligatory alms are meant, and Ibn Jurayj's that voluntary giving is included too, which al-Balkhi chose and al-Tabrisi calls stronger for being more general [4]. Fayd Kashani finds the day of death the more apparent reading [17]. Tabatabai reads the command as the tail of the preceding verses on fighting and giving, revealed with them [1].

Then the Throne Verse. Nothing intercedes with Him except by His leave, and none grasps His knowledge except as He wills. Al-Tusi gathers four senses of al-Qayyum: the One who stands over every soul with what it has earned, the everlasting, the One who manages His creation, and the Knowing [9].

Then the turn: there is no compulsion in religion. Tabatabai holds that coercion works only on outward acts and bodily movement, while belief is a matter of the heart that compulsion cannot rule [3]. Al-Tabrisi reports that Ibn Masud and Ibn Zayd held the verse abrogated by the verse of the sword, while the rest hold it firm [6], and al-Tusi lists five readings of the fake deities: Satan, the soothsayer, the sorcerer, the rebels among jinn and men, and idols [10]. The passage closes on guardianship: al-Tabrisi describes God's wilaya of the faithful as help in establishing the proof, victory over their enemy, and reward for obedience [7].

note.en: Al-Tusi holds that 'nor intercession' is general in its wording but specific in what is meant, a point he reports without disagreement; the Shia deny intercession to the faithless outright [8].
On 'His seat', al-Tusi reports Ibn Abbas's gloss that the kursi is His knowledge, and says the same is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قلت لأبي عبد الله (عليه السلام): قوله تعالى: { مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ … نحن أولئك الشافعون
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, with his chain

text.en: I said to Abu Abdillah: the words of God, 'Who is it that may intercede with Him except with His permission?' He said: We are those intercessors.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عن قول الله جل و عز: { وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ … بل الكرسي وسع السماوات و الأرض و العرش، و كل شي وسع الكرسي
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Thalaba ibn Maymun, from Zurara ibn Ayan

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about 'His seat embraces the heavens and the earth': do the heavens and the earth embrace the seat, or does the seat embrace them? He said: Rather the seat embraces the heavens and the earth and the throne, and the seat embraces everything.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: من قرأ آية الكرسي مرة صرف الله عنه ألف مكروه من مكاره الدنيا وألف مكروه من مكاره الآخرة أيسر مكروه الدنيا الفقر وأيسر مكروه الآخرة عذاب القبر

text.en: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi once, God turns away from him a thousand of the hardships of this world and a thousand of the hardships of the next. The least hardship of this world is poverty, and the least of the next is the punishment of the grave.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi reports occasions: from Mujahid, that an Ansari was forcing his slave Subayh to Islam; from Ibn Abbas, that Ansari sons among Banu al-Nadir were given the choice when the tribe was expelled [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، في قول الله عز و جل: { فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ … هي الإيمان بالله وحده لا شريك له
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, both from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: On the words of God, 'has held fast to the firmest handle', he said: It is faith in God alone, who has no partner.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وعن الباقر عليه السلام هو مودتنا أهل البيت

text.en: The firmest handle is love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: من أحب أن يستمسك بالعروة الوثقى التي لا انفصام لها، فليستمسك بولاية أخي و وصيي علي بن أبي طالب، فانه لا يهلك من أحبه و تولاه، و لا ينجو من أبغضه و عاداه
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-Amash, from Abaya ibn Ribi, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas

text.en: Whoever wishes to hold fast to the firmest handle, for which there is no breaking, let him hold fast to the wilaya of my brother and my successor Ali ibn Abi Talib. Whoever loves him and takes him as guardian does not perish, and whoever hates him and opposes him is not saved.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا دين لمن دان الله بولاية إمام جائر ليس من الله، و لا عتب على من دان بولاية إمام عادل من الله … يعني من ظلمات الذنوب إلى نور التوبة و المغفرة، بولايتهم كل إمام عادل من الله
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Yafur

text.en: No religion for one who serves God through allegiance to a tyrannical imam not from God, and no blame on one who serves through allegiance to a just imam from God. He brings them out of the darkness of sins into the light of repentance and forgiveness, by allegiance to every just imam.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: المؤمن يتقلب في خمسة من النور مدخله نور ومخرجه نور وعلمه نور وكلامه نور ومنظره يوم القيامة النور
narrations.chain: al-Sadiq, from his fathers, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: The believer moves about in five things of light: his entrance is light, his exit is light, his knowledge is light, his speech is light, and his sight on the Day of Resurrection is light.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: النور آل محمد عليهم السلام والظلمات عدوهم

text.en: The light is the family of Muhammad, and the darkness is their enemy.

perspectives.en: On 'He brings them out of darkness into light' the two traditions part. Al-Tabari reports Qatada's gloss, out of misguidance into guidance, with the fake deities read as Satan [23]. Al-Qurtubi carries Mujahid's reading that the verse was revealed about people who believed in Jesus and rejected Muhammad, and Ibn Atiyya's reply that the wording needs no such restriction [31]. Al-Tusi knows a reading of the verse as apostasy from Islam and rejects it as unfitting for the Shia school, since a believer does not truly apostatize [11]. In al-Burhan, Imam al-Sadiq reads the pair as allegiance: sins to repentance under a just imam, Islam to darkness under a tyrant [16].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فهذا كله يؤيد أن يكون هاتان الآيتان ذيل الآيات السابقة، والجميع نازلة معاً

sources.gloss: All of this supports that these two verses are the tail of the preceding verses, and that all of them came down together.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والاعتقاد والإِيمان من الأمور القلبية التي لا يحكم فيها الإِكراه والإِجبار، فإن الإِكراه إنما يؤثر في الأعمال الظاهرية والأفعال والحركات البدنية المادية

sources.gloss: Belief and faith are matters of the heart, in which coercion and compulsion have no rule, for coercion acts only on outward deeds and bodily movements.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل أراد به الفرض كالزكاة ونحوها دون النفل لاقتران الوعيد به عن الحسن ولأن ظاهر الأمر يقتضي الإيجاب وقيل يدخل فيه النفل والفرض عن ابن جريج، واختاره البلخي وهو الأقوى لأنه أعم

sources.gloss: It is said that the obligatory is meant, such as alms and the like, not the voluntary, on the authority of Hasan; and it is said that voluntary and obligatory alike are included, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, which al-Balkhi chose and which is stronger because it is more general.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر قال: من قرأ آية الكرسي مرة صرف الله عنه ألف مكروه من مكاره الدنيا وألف مكروه من مكاره الآخرة

sources.gloss: It is narrated from Abu Jafar al-Baqir: whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi once, God turns away from him a thousand of the hardships of this world and a thousand of the hardships of the next.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهكذا قال ابن مسعود وابن زيد أنها منسوخة بآية السيف وقال الباقون هي محكمة

sources.gloss: Likewise Ibn Masud and Ibn Zayd said that it is abrogated by the verse of the sword, and the rest said it stands firm.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: تعالى ولي المؤمنين على ثلاثة أوجه: أحدها: إنه يتولاهم بالمعونة على إقامة الحجة والبرهان لـهم في هدايتهم

sources.gloss: He is the guardian of the faithful in three respects. The first: He takes charge of them by helping them establish the proof and the evidence for their guidance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإن كان على لفظ العموم فالمراد به الخصوص بلا خلاف

sources.gloss: Though its wording is general, what is meant by it is particular, without disagreement.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل في معنى القيوم، أربعة أقوال

sources.gloss: Four views have been stated on the meaning of al-Qayyum.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { ومن يكفر بالطاغوت } قيل فيه خمسة أقوال: أحدها - ما روي عن عمر، ومجاهد، وقتادة: أنه الشيطان

sources.gloss: On 'one who disavows fake deities', five views have been stated. The first, narrated from Umar, Mujahid and Qatada, is that it is Satan.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال مجاهد: إنه في قوم ارتدّوا عن الاسلام، والاول أليق بمذهبنا، لأن عندنا لا يجوز أن يرتد المؤمن على الحقيقة

sources.gloss: Mujahid said it concerns a people who apostatized from Islam; but the first answer is more fitting with our school, because in our view a believer cannot truly apostatize.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نحن أولئك الشافعون

sources.gloss: We are those intercessors.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يعني من ظلمات الذنوب إلى نور التوبة و المغفرة، بولايتهم كل إمام عادل من الله

sources.gloss: That is, out of the darkness of sins into the light of repentance and forgiveness, by their allegiance to every just imam from God.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد به يوم الموت كما مرّ في قوله عز وجل واتّقوا يوماً لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئاً وهو اظهر

sources.gloss: It may be that the day of death is meant, as came earlier in His words, 'Beware of the day when no soul will compensate for another', and this is the more apparent sense.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وعن الباقر عليه السلام هو مودتنا أهل البيت

sources.gloss: And from al-Baqir: it is love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في الكافي عن الصادق عليه السلام النور آل محمد عليهم السلام والظلمات عدوهم

sources.gloss: In al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq: the light is the family of Muhammad, and the darkness is their enemy.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن قتادة قوله: { اللهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إلى النُّورِ } يقول: من الضلالة إلى الهدى { وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أوْلِياؤُهُمْ الطَّاغُوتُ } الشيطان

sources.gloss: From Qatada on 'Allah is the wali of the faithful: He brings them out of darkness into light', he says: out of misguidance into guidance; and 'as for the faithless, their awliya are the fake deities', that is, Satan.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وقال مجاهد وعبدة بن أبي لُبَابة: قوله «اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا» نزلت في قوم آمنوا بعيسى فلما جاء محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم كفروا به، فذلك إخراجهم من النور إلى الظلمات

sources.gloss: Mujahid and Abda ibn Abi Lubaba said: 'Allah is the wali of the faithful' came down about a people who believed in Jesus, then disbelieved in Muhammad when he came; that is their being brought out of light into darkness.

title.en: Who gives life and brings death

essay.en:
Three scenes, one question: who gives life and who brings death. Al-Mizan notes that these verses carry the meaning of tawhid and are not cut off from what precedes them [1].

The first is an argument. Al-Tabrisi reads it as consolation for the Prophet after the declaration that God is the guardian of the faithful, and names the king Nimrod ibn Kanan, the first tyrant to claim lordship [2]. His counter-claim meant freeing one condemned man and killing another; al-Tusi says he seized the wording and let the meaning go, since the argument was about originating life [5]. Abraham turns to the sun, which al-Safi calls a move from a hidden instance to a plain one, not a retreat to a second proof [14]. The king is dumbfounded.

The second argues by demonstration. Al-Tusi reports the traveller as Uzayr, narrated from Abu Abdillah, and as Irmiya, narrated from Abu Jafar, and the township as Bayt al-Maqdis after Bukhtnassar ruined it [6]. A hundred years pass for him as a day; his food, his drink and his own bones are the proof. Kufa and Sham read nunshizuha, the Hijaz and Basra nunshiruha [3].

The third is a request. Al-Tusi holds the strongest view to be that Abraham wanted to see what he already knew by inference, and reads 'in order that my heart may be at rest' as certainty added to certainty [7]. The birds are cut, scattered and called back, and the passage closes on a power that is God's alone.

note.en: 'Only because Allah had given him kingdom': al-Tusi distinguishes wealth and ample circumstance, which God may give believer or disbeliever alike, from command over people's affairs, which He does not hand to the misguided [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) قال له: أحيى من قتلته إن كنت صادقا

text.en: Abraham said to him: Revive the one you killed, if you are truthful.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن أشد الناس عذابا يوم القيامة سبعة نفر: أولهم ابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه، و نمرود بن كنعان الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Hannan ibn Sadir, from a man among the companions of Abu Abdillah

text.en: The most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection are seven: the first of them is the son of Adam who killed his brother, and Nimrod ibn Kanan who argued with Abraham about his Lord.

note.en: Al-Safi takes 'the bones' as the man's own, and nunshizuha as raising them one upon another for reassembly; read with ra, nunshiruha, it means reviving them [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فقالوا له راجع ربك فقل له ما ذنب الفقراء والمساكين والضعفاء … ثم أوحى الله تعالى إليه قل لهم لأنكم رأيتم المنكر فلم تنكروه
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: They said to him: Go back to your Lord and ask Him what sin the poor, the destitute and the weak have committed. ... Then God revealed to him: Tell them, it is because you saw the wrong and did not forbid it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فخرج أرميا على حماره ومعه تبين قد تزوّده وشيء من عصير فنظر إلى سباع البر وسباع البحر وسباع الجو تأكل تلك الجيف ففكّر في نفسه ساعة ثم قال انى يحيي الله هؤلاء وقد أكلتهم السباع فأماته الله مكانه … وبقي ارميا ميتاً ماءة سنة ثم أحياه الله فأوّل ما احيى الله منه عينيه
narrations.chain: al-Qummi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: Irmiya went out on his donkey and saw the beasts of land, sea and air eating those carcasses. He thought a while, then said: How will God revive these when the beasts have eaten them? So God made him die on the spot. ... He lay dead a hundred years, then God revived him, his eyes first.

note.en: Abu Jafar, Hamza, Khalaf and Ruways read fasirhunna with kasra, the rest fasurhunna with damma; the verb carries both inclining them to you and cutting them [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: سئل الرضا عليه السلام كان في قلبه شك قال لا كان على يقين ولكنه اراد الله الزيادة في يقينه

text.en: Al-Rida was asked: Was there doubt in his heart? He said: No, he was upon certainty, but God wanted an increase in his certainty.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: و هذه آية متشابهة، و معناها: أنه سأل عن الكيفية، و الكيفية من فعل الله عز و جل، متى لم يعلمها العالم لم يلحقه عيب، و لا عرض في توحيده نقص
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq, from Hamza ibn al-Qasim al-Alawi, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Zayyat, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad

text.en: This is an ambiguous verse. Its meaning is that he asked about the modality, and modality belongs to the act of God; when a knower does not know it, no fault attaches to him and no deficiency touches his tawhid.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فأخذ إبراهيم عليه السلام الطاووس والديك والحمام والغراب فقال الله عزوجل: { فصرهن إليك } ، أي قطعهن ثم اخلط لحمهن وفرقهن على عشرة جبال ثم خذ مناقيرهن وادعهن يأتينك سعياً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Abraham took the peacock, the rooster, the dove and the crow. God said: 'Cut them up', then mix their flesh and divide them over ten mountains, then take their beaks and call them, and they will come to you hastening.

perspectives.en: The traditions differ twice. On the traveller, Ibn Kathir reports from Ali ibn Abi Talib and others that he was Uzayr and calls this the well known view [20]; al-Tusi carries Uzayr from Abu Abdillah but also Irmiya from Abu Jafar [6], and the narration al-Safi gives at length is Irmiya's [14]. On Abraham's request, al-Qurtubi reports that the majority denied any doubt, yet that al-Tabari preferred the reading that he asked because he doubted God's power [24]. Al-Tusi calls that reading false [7], and al-Rida, asked whether doubt was in Abraham's heart, answered no [15].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الآيات مشتملة على معنى التوحيد ولذلك كانت غير خالية عن الارتباط بما قبلها من الآيات فمن المحتمل أن تكون نازلة معها.

sources.gloss: The verses carry the meaning of tawhid, and for that reason they are not free of connection with the verses before them, so it is possible that they were revealed together with them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: تسلية لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم قصّ عليه بعده قصة إبراهيم ونمرود

sources.gloss: As a consolation for His Prophet, He recounted to him after that the story of Abraham and Nimrod.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة نُنشرها بضم النون الأولى وبالراء وقرأ أهل الكوفة والشام نَنْشُزُها بالزاي

sources.gloss: The readers of the Hijaz and Basra read nunshiruha, with a damma on the first nun and with ra, and the readers of Kufa and Sham read nunshizuha, with zay.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة وخلف ورويس عن يعقوب فَصِرهن بكسر الصاد والباقون فَصُرهن بضم الصاد

sources.gloss: Abu Jafar, Hamza, Khalaf and Ruways from Yaqub read fasirhunna with a kasra on the sad, and the rest read fasurhunna with a damma.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدهما - يكون بكثرة المال واتساع الحال، فهذا يجوز أن ينعم الله (عزّ وجل) به على أحد من مؤمن وكافر، كما قال في قصة بني إسرائيل: { وجعلكم ملوكاً وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحداً من العالمين } والثاني - ملك بتمليك الأمر والنهي والتدبير لأمور الناس، فهذا لا يجوز أن يجعله الله لأهل الضلال

sources.gloss: One kind is abundance of wealth and ample circumstance, and God may bestow this on anyone, believer or disbeliever, as He said in the story of the Children of Israel: 'and made you kings and gave you what He had not given to anyone in the world'. The second is kingship by holding command, prohibition and the management of people's affairs, and this God does not grant to the people of misguidance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال قتادة والربيع: الذي مر على قرية هو عزير، وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله (ع). وقال وهب بن منبه: هو أرميا، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر (ع).

sources.gloss: Qatada and al-Rabi said the one who passed by the township was Uzayr, and that is narrated from Abu Abdillah. Wahb ibn Munabbih said he was Irmiya, and that is what is narrated from Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال قوم: إنما سأله، لأنه أحب أن يعلم ذلك علم عيان بعد أن كان عالماً به من جهة الاستدلال. وهو أقوى الوجوه.

sources.gloss: Some said he asked only because he wished to know it with the knowledge of direct sight after having known it by inference, and this is the strongest of the views.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قل لهم لأنكم رأيتم المنكر فلم تنكروه

sources.gloss: Tell them: it is because you saw the wrong and did not forbid it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فأخذ إبراهيم عليه السلام الطاووس والديك والحمام والغراب فقال الله عزوجل: { فصرهن إليك } ، أي قطعهن

sources.gloss: So Abraham took the peacock, the rooster, the dove and the crow, and God said: 'Cut them up', that is, cut them into pieces.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) قال له: أحيى من قتلته إن كنت صادقا

sources.gloss: Abraham said to him: Revive the one you killed, if you are truthful.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنه سأل عن الكيفية، و الكيفية من فعل الله عز و جل، متى لم يعلمها العالم لم يلحقه عيب، و لا عرض في توحيده نقص

sources.gloss: He asked about the modality, and the modality is of God's own doing; when a learned man does not know it, no fault attaches to him and no deficiency occurs in his tawhid.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وهو في الحقيقة عدول عن مثال خفي إلى مثال جلّي من مقدوراته التي يعجز عن الاتيان بها غيره لا عن حجة إلى أخرى

sources.gloss: In reality it is a turn from a hidden instance to a plain one among the things in His power that no one else is able to bring, not a turn from one proof to another.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: سئل الرضا عليه السلام كان في قلبه شك قال لا كان على يقين ولكنه اراد الله الزيادة في يقينه

sources.gloss: Al-Rida was asked: was there doubt in his heart? He said: No, he was upon certainty, but God wanted an increase in his certainty.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: عن ناجية بن كعب، عن علي بن أبي طالب، أنه قال هو عزير. ورواه ابن جرير عن ناجية نفسه، وحكاه ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والسدي وسليمان بن بريدة، وهذا القول هو المشهور.

sources.gloss: From Naji ibn Kab, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: he is Uzayr. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Naji himself, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi and Sulayman ibn Burayda, and this view is the well known one.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وترجم الطبريّ في تفسيره فقال: وقال آخرون سأل ذلك ربّه لأنه شك في قدرة الله تعالىٰ

sources.gloss: Al-Tabari headed a section in his tafsir saying: others said he asked that of his Lord because he doubted the power of God.

essay.en:
Six verses, one lesson. Tabatabai reads them as revealed together, a single call to the faithful to spend in the way of Allah [1].

It opens with arithmetic turned into a picture: one grain that grows seven ears, each ear a hundred grains. Tusi reports al-Rabi and al-Suddi restricting that seven hundred to spending in the way of Allah, with other good deeds at ten [8]; Tabrisi holds the verse general over every door of righteousness and reports that reading from Abu Abdillah [2].

Then comes the condition. The gift must not be followed by reproach or affront: by saying did I not give you, did I not enrich you, or by wishing the poor man out of one's life [3]. Tusi finds here no proof that a settled reward is cancelled later; the promise was conditional from the start, so when the condition fails nothing was ever owed [9].

A kind word and forgiveness outrank a charity that ends in injury. Allah is rich, free of need for what you give; He called you to it only to benefit you, and He is forbearing, not hurrying to punish [10].

Three pictures close the argument: soil on a smooth rock, stripped bare by a single downpour; a garden on a hillside that yields whether the rain is heavy or light; and a burnt orchard belonging to an old man with small children. The passage does not name whom the last one is for. It hands the reader the picture and asks him to reflect.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
